records.name: MilkRun
records.failure_reason: Unsustainable Unit Economics
records.investors: AirTree Ventures, Blackbird Ventures, Tiger Global, Grok Ventures
records.lesson: Sydney's quick-commerce darling raised AUD$75M+ then collapsed inside 18 months when capital tightened. Australian density couldn't support 10-minute grocery economics.

records.name: Send
records.failure_reason: Quick-Commerce Collapse
records.lesson: Smaller Australian quick-commerce competitor that collapsed before MilkRun, signaling the entire category's unviability locally.

records.name: Metigy
records.failure_reason: Cash Burn & Founder Issues
records.investors: Cygnet Capital, Regal Funds, Five V Capital
records.lesson: Sydney AI-marketing platform raised AUD$28M then collapsed amid allegations the founder used company funds for personal property. A governance failure case study.

records.name: Volt Bank
records.failure_reason: Could Not Raise Series F
records.lesson: Australia's first neobank to receive a banking licence handed it back in 2022 after failing to raise the AUD$200M needed to become profitable.

records.name: Brighte (Down Round)
records.failure_reason: Rates & BNPL Reckoning
records.investors: Atlassian co-founder Mike Cannon-Brookes (Grok), Airtree, Skip Capital
records.lesson: Australia's solar-financing BNPL hit the same wall as global BNPL: rising rates, rising defaults, no path to profitability at peak valuation.

records.name: Plenti (Stock Collapse)
records.failure_reason: Margin Compression & Equity Collapse
records.lesson: ASX-listed Plenti's stock fell over 80% as Australian P2P lending margins evaporated under the rate cycle.

records.name: Olive AI
records.failure_reason: Overpromised RPA as 'AI', under-delivered ROI to hospitals
records.investors: Vista Equity, Tiger Global, General Catalyst, Base10, Drive Capital
records.lesson: Selling AI to hospitals requires proven ROI per workflow, not a $4B narrative. Olive's automation broke on messy edge cases and clients cancelled.

records.name: Arrival
records.failure_reason: Microfactory model never produced vehicles at scale
records.lesson: 'Microfactories' sound capital-light in a pitch deck. In reality auto manufacturing rewards scale, and Arrival never built one.

records.name: Argo AI
records.failure_reason: Backers Ford and VW pulled the plug on robotaxi timeline
records.lesson: When your only two customers stop believing L4 arrives this decade, no independent balance sheet survives it.

records.name: Iron Ox
records.failure_reason: Robotic greenhouse capex could not beat commodity produce prices
records.investors: Y Combinator, Crosslink, Eniac, R7, Amplo
records.lesson: Robotics + agriculture forces you to compete on lettuce price. Automation gains rarely offset the extra capital cost of the greenhouse.

records.name: Veev
records.failure_reason: Modular home factory economics broke as housing demand cooled
records.investors: LennarX, Zeev Ventures, JLL Spark, Zeev, Fifth Wall
records.lesson: Modular housing has killed serial unicorns — Katerra, Veev — because factory throughput doesn't beat conventional builders once demand drops.

records.name: Electric Last Mile Solutions
records.failure_reason: SEC probe, founder exits, and unable to raise more capital
records.lesson: Post-SPAC EV plays with unresolved SEC issues can't raise follow-on capital. ELMS ran out of runway in 18 months.

records.name: Hopin
records.failure_reason: Pandemic tailwind evaporated overnight, valuation cratered
records.investors: IVP, Andreessen Horowitz, Tiger Global, General Catalyst, Coatue
records.lesson: A pandemic tailwind is not a durable market. Hopin raised at $7.75B in a category that shrank 80% once offices reopened.

records.name: Thrasio
records.failure_reason: Bought Amazon brands at 2021 multiples, couldn't service debt
records.investors: Silver Lake, Advent, Oaktree, PEAK6, Upper90
records.lesson: Aggregators paid 5x EBITDA for FBA brands in 2021. When Amazon fees rose and ad costs doubled, the debt stack sank them all.

records.name: Perch
records.failure_reason: Aggregator model collapsed, sold to Razor Group in distress
records.lesson: Perch was the 'quality' Amazon roll-up. When rates rose, quality didn't matter — every aggregator got repriced together.

records.name: Frank (JPMorgan)
records.failure_reason: Founder Charlie Javice convicted of $175M JPMorgan sale fraud
records.investors: Aleph, Marc Rowan, Apollo (angel), Chris Sacca
records.lesson: The most spectacular startup failures aren't insolvencies — they're founder-driven fraud that unwinds a nine-figure acquisition.

records.name: Purplebricks
records.failure_reason: Flat-fee model couldn't cover marketing spend as UK market cooled
records.investors: Neil Woodford, Axel Springer, public shareholders (LSE:PURP)
records.lesson: In real estate, £1,000-flat-fee revenue can't fund £70M TV campaigns — the LTV/CAC math breaks the moment listings slow.

records.name: Shift Technologies
records.failure_reason: Used-car e-commerce economics broke, merger with CarLotz failed
records.investors: DCM, Goldman Sachs, DFJ, Highland Capital, Great Oaks
records.lesson: Consolidating two failing used-car startups doesn't create a winning one — it doubles operational drag.

records.name: Reali
records.failure_reason: Cash-offer / power-buyer model unworkable as rates spiked
records.lesson: Power-buyer models depend on cheap capital and stable prices. When mortgage rates doubled in 2022, every buy-before-sell player broke.

records.name: Enjoy Technology
records.failure_reason: Home-visit retail model unprofitable, Apple contract insufficient
records.investors: Kleiner Perkins, Highland Capital, Andreessen Horowitz, Marvin Traub
records.lesson: Ex-Apple retail chief Ron Johnson learned twice (JCPenney, Enjoy) that reinventing retail from famous credentials still requires unit economics.

records.name: BuzzFeed News
records.failure_reason: Pulitzer-winning newsroom couldn't outrun ad revenue collapse
records.lesson: Prestige journalism does not monetize on programmatic ads. BuzzFeed News won a Pulitzer and was still shuttered.

records.name: Vice Media
records.failure_reason: Once valued at $5.7B, filed Chapter 11 in 2023 and shuttered flagship site in 2024
records.investors: Disney, TPG, Sixth Street, Fortress, A&E
records.lesson: A cool brand, a $5.7B valuation, and a TV network still can't survive if programmatic ads and Facebook traffic evaporate together.

records.name: Volta Charging
records.failure_reason: Ad-subsidized charging model unproven, sold to Shell for $169M
records.lesson: 'Free' charging paid by ad impressions on the station screen was a beautiful pitch. It never actually paid for the electrons.

records.name: Adept AI
records.failure_reason: Founding team acqui-hired by Amazon; company left as licensor
records.investors: General Catalyst, Spark Capital, Greylock, Microsoft, Nvidia
records.lesson: The 2024 AI 'reverse acqui-hire' invented a new failure mode: the company survives on paper while its brain moves to Big Tech.

records.name: Inflection AI (original)
records.failure_reason: Microsoft hired Mustafa Suleyman and team, gutting the original consumer plan
records.investors: Microsoft, Nvidia, Reid Hoffman, Bill Gates, Eric Schmidt
records.lesson: A $1.5B raise doesn't guarantee a business — sometimes the best exit is your investor hiring your founders directly.

records.name: Character.AI (original)
records.failure_reason: Google hired founders and licensed tech; consumer plan effectively over
records.lesson: The third 2024 reverse acqui-hire — Google-Character followed Microsoft-Inflection and Amazon-Adept, formalizing a new category of AI failure.

records.name: Convoy
records.failure_reason: Digital freight brokerage margins vanished in freight recession
records.investors: Generation IM, T. Rowe Price, Y Combinator, Bezos Expeditions
records.lesson: Freight brokerage is a spread business. When the freight cycle turns, the spread turns negative for everyone chasing GMV.

records.name: Hyperloop One
records.failure_reason: Ten years, one test track, zero commercial route
records.investors: DP World, Richard Branson (Virgin), Sherpa Capital, GE Ventures
records.lesson: The most seductive hardware pitches (500 mph vacuum tubes) still need regulatory reality and cost per mile below rail.

records.name: Divvy Homes
records.failure_reason: Rent-to-own economics broken by rates; sold to Brookfield at half valuation
records.investors: Tiger Global, GGV, Andreessen Horowitz, Caffeinated Capital
records.lesson: Even the 'right' rent-to-own model at $2B valuation had to sell to Brookfield for half that. Housing beta ate the alpha.

records.name: Rally (Rally Rd)
records.failure_reason: Fractional collectibles secondary market never had liquidity
records.investors: Upfront Ventures, Alexis Ohanian, Anthos Capital, Porsche Ventures
records.lesson: Fractional collectibles work as a marketing gimmick, not as a liquid secondary market. Every player in the category has stalled.

records.name: Argo Blockchain (US Mining ops)
records.failure_reason: Sold flagship Helios Texas facility to Galaxy Digital to avoid Chapter 11
records.lesson: Bitcoin mining is a leveraged bet on hashprice. When BTC halved and energy prices doubled in 2022, over-levered miners had to sell flagship assets to survive.

records.name: Core Scientific
records.failure_reason: BTC crash + Celsius exposure forced Chapter 11
records.investors: Ascend Capital, XMS Capital, public shareholders
records.lesson: Public miners that lent hashrate to Celsius discovered the counter-party risk when Celsius defaulted mid-2022. The debt stack did the rest.

records.name: Compute North
records.failure_reason: Debt-financed data center build tripped when BTC crashed and Compute North's own customers defaulted
records.investors: Generate Capital, Marathon Digital, National Grid Partners
records.lesson: Crypto data center capex is only cheap if BTC and hashprice stay high. Compute North built through 2022 and never recovered.

records.name: Olist (Down Round & Layoffs)
records.failure_reason: Macro Reversal & Profitability Push
records.lesson: Brazil's 2021 unicorns face a brutal 2023-24 reality: SoftBank-funded growth collapsed when capital tightened and Olist-style marketplaces had to cut deep.

records.name: Loft (Down Round)
records.failure_reason: iBuying Model & Brazilian Rates
records.investors: SoftBank, Andreessen Horowitz, D1 Capital, Tiger Global
records.lesson: Brazilian iBuying never made sense at 13% interest rates. Loft's $2.9B peak valuation collapsed as the inventory model bled cash.

records.name: Facily
records.failure_reason: Unsustainable Unit Economics
records.lesson: Brazil's answer to Pinduoduo couldn't replicate the Chinese model's logistics density. Group-buying with subsidies burned $300M before shutdown.

records.name: Vnda (Closed)
records.failure_reason: Acquired & Sunsetted
records.lesson: Brazilian e-commerce SaaS Vnda was acquired by Olist at the 2021 peak — only to be shut down two years later when the parent company restructured.

records.name: Kavak (Brazil Exit)
records.failure_reason: Capital-Intensive Inventory Model
records.lesson: Even with $1.5B raised, Kavak couldn't make Brazilian used-car economics work and exited the country in 2023.

records.name: Buggy
records.failure_reason: Unviable Inventory Economics
records.lesson: A smaller used-car play that ran into the same inventory wall as Kavak — but with one-tenth the cushion.

records.name: Yellow (Grow Mobility)
records.failure_reason: Unit Economics & COVID
records.lesson: Brazil's biggest bike-and-scooter sharing startup couldn't reach unit economics, then COVID sealed its fate.

records.name: Easynvest (Sold at Discount)
records.failure_reason: Outcompeted by XP & Nubank
records.lesson: Easynvest pioneered Brazilian discount brokerage but was outscaled by XP Inc and folded into Nubank at a price below its 2018 mark.

records.name: Wealthsimple (Down Round)
records.failure_reason: Crypto Winter & Margin Compression
records.investors: Power Corporation, TCV, Allianz X, Greylock
records.lesson: Canada's flagship fintech raised at CAD$5B in 2021, then accepted a CAD$1.5B mark in 2023 — destroying CAD$3.5B+ in paper value.

records.name: Tehama (Wind-Down)
records.failure_reason: Post-COVID Demand Collapse
records.lesson: Ottawa-based virtual-desktop startup Tehama was a COVID darling that couldn't sustain growth as remote-work tooling consolidated.

records.name: Thinkific (Stock Collapse)
records.failure_reason: Post-COVID Demand Decline
records.lesson: Vancouver-based Thinkific listed on the TSX in 2021 then lost over 90% of its market cap as creator-economy spending collapsed.

records.name: ApplyBoard (Down Round & Layoffs)
records.failure_reason: Visa Policy Risk & Layoffs
records.investors: Ontario Teachers, Drive Capital, Garage Capital
records.lesson: Canada's CAD$3.2B unicorn ApplyBoard accepted a deep recap and laid off ~40% of staff as Canadian student-visa caps decimated its core market.

records.name: Lightspeed Commerce (Value Destruction)
records.failure_reason: Short Report & Stock Collapse
records.lesson: Montreal-based Lightspeed peaked at CAD$30B in 2021 then lost over 80% after short-seller accusations. While still operating, billions in shareholder value evaporated.

records.name: Delphia
records.failure_reason: SEC Settlement & Wind-Down
records.lesson: Toronto AI-investing startup paid an SEC fine for AI-washing claims, then wound down — a fintech case of overstating AI capabilities.

records.name: Mt. Gox
records.failure_reason: Hack & Mismanagement
records.lesson: Handling other people's money requires enterprise-grade security and compliance, not hobbyist infrastructure. Mt. Gox proved that being first-to-market means nothing if you can't protect customer assets.

records.name: BitConnect
records.failure_reason: Ponzi Scheme
records.lesson: Guaranteed returns in volatile markets are the hallmark of fraud. BitConnect's promised 1% daily returns were mathematically impossible and classic Ponzi mechanics.

records.name: QuadrigaCX
records.failure_reason: Fraud & Mysterious Death of Founder
records.lesson: Single points of failure — especially a single person controlling all private keys — create existential risk. QuadrigaCX showed that 'key man risk' can be literal.

records.name: Wirecard
records.failure_reason: Massive Accounting Fraud
records.lesson: Even DAX-30 companies with Big Four auditors can be complete frauds. Wirecard proved that regulatory capture and national pride can blind everyone to obvious red flags.

records.name: Greensill Capital
records.failure_reason: Concentrated Risk & Insurance Loss
records.lesson: Supply chain finance works when risk is diversified. Greensill concentrated exposure on a few troubled borrowers and relied on a single insurer — creating a house of cards.

records.name: BitMEX
records.failure_reason: Regulatory Evasion & Criminal Charges
records.lesson: You cannot build a financial empire by deliberately evading regulations. BitMEX's founders chose offshore structures over compliance and paid with criminal convictions.

records.name: N26 US
records.failure_reason: Regulatory Failures & Market Misfit
records.investors: Third Point Ventures, Coatue, Insight Partners, Peter Thiel, Tencent
records.lesson: European fintech success doesn't automatically translate to the US market. N26's failure in America shows that regulatory environments, competitive landscapes, and customer expectations differ dramatically.

records.name: Health IQ
records.failure_reason: Fraud — Fabricated Metrics & False Claims
records.investors: Andreessen Horowitz, Ribbit Capital, Aquiline Capital Partners
records.lesson: Insurance is a heavily regulated industry where fabricated data doesn't just mislead investors — it violates insurance regulations. Health IQ's founder couldn't fake actuarial science.

records.name: Vicarious
records.failure_reason: Over-ambition & No Product-Market Fit
records.investors: Mark Zuckerberg, Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos, Founders Fund, Khosla Ventures
records.lesson: Having the most famous investors in the world cannot compensate for failing to ship a product. Vicarious spent 12 years chasing artificial general intelligence without finding a commercial application.

records.name: Kindred AI
records.failure_reason: Failed Commercialization
records.investors: Google Ventures, Horizons Ventures, Eclipse Ventures
records.lesson: Building AI robots that learn from human demonstrations is brilliant research but requires massive scale to become economically viable. Kindred never found enough customers to justify the R&D investment.

records.name: Outdoor Voices
records.failure_reason: Founder Drama & Unsustainable Spending
records.investors: General Catalyst, GV (Google Ventures), Forerunner Ventures, J.Crew's Mickey Drexler
records.lesson: A beloved brand with a passionate community can still fail if the business burns cash faster than it generates revenue. Outdoor Voices proved that Instagram-worthy branding doesn't equal a sustainable business.

records.name: HQ Trivia
records.failure_reason: Founder Death, No Revenue Model & User Decline
records.lesson: A viral moment isn't a business model. HQ Trivia captured lightning in a bottle but never figured out how to monetize it, and the death of its co-founder accelerated a spiral that was already underway.

records.name: Ozy Media
records.failure_reason: Fabricated Metrics & Fraud
records.investors: Axel Springer, Laurene Powell Jobs, Marc Lasry
records.lesson: In media, inflated metrics are easy to fabricate and hard to verify. Ozy's CEO impersonated a YouTube executive on a Goldman Sachs due diligence call — the moment fraud crossed from deception into delusion.

records.name: Frank (JPMorgan Fraud)
records.failure_reason: Fabricated User Data — $175M Acquisition Fraud
records.investors: Aleph, Reach Capital, Chegg, Marc Rowan
records.lesson: When JPMorgan Chase — the largest bank in the world — can be defrauded by a startup founder who fabricated 4 million fake users, it proves that acquisition due diligence failures exist at every level.

records.name: Zenefits
records.failure_reason: Compliance Violations & Hypergrowth Chaos
records.investors: Andreessen Horowitz, Fidelity, TPG, Insight Ventures
records.lesson: Zenefits grew at 'break-neck speed' by selling insurance without proper licenses — proving that in regulated industries, compliance isn't a growth constraint to hack around.

records.name: Rethink Robotics
records.failure_reason: Over-engineering & Market Mismatch
records.investors: Bezos Expeditions, CRV, Highland Capital Partners, GE Ventures
records.lesson: Collaborative robots are a brilliant concept, but Rethink's Baxter was too slow and imprecise for manufacturing, and too expensive for its target market of small manufacturers.

records.name: Faraday Future
records.failure_reason: Founder Fraud, Governance Failures & Endless Delays
records.investors: Public markets (SPAC), Ares Management, Birch Lake Partners
records.lesson: Faraday Future is what happens when a founder wanted by Chinese authorities for fraud convinces American investors to fund a car company that barely produces any cars.

records.name: DataRobot
records.failure_reason: Commoditization & Failed Enterprise Pivot
records.investors: Sapphire Ventures, Iconiq, T. Rowe Price, Tiger Global, Mubadala
records.lesson: AutoML was a brilliant concept when data science was scarce. But as AI tools became ubiquitous and cloud providers offered their own AutoML, DataRobot's $6.3B valuation evaporated.

records.name: Clarifai
records.failure_reason: Commoditization by Cloud AI APIs
records.investors: New Enterprise Associates, Union Square Ventures, LDV Capital, Nvidia
records.lesson: Clarifai built world-class computer vision when it was novel. Then Google, Amazon, and Microsoft offered the same thing as a $1-per-1000-images API call, destroying the premium market.

records.name: x.ai (Scheduling AI)
records.failure_reason: AI Couldn't Replace Calendar Coordination
records.investors: Two Sigma, Work-Bench, Firsthand Technology, Pritzker Group
records.lesson: Scheduling meetings seems simple but involves nuanced human preferences that early AI couldn't handle. x.ai spent $44M and 7 years on a problem that calendar links solved for free.

records.name: Mighty AI
records.failure_reason: Race to Bottom in Training Data
records.investors: Foundry Group, Madrona Venture Group, Intel Capital
records.lesson: Training data labeling was critical for AI development but became a commodity service where price — not quality — won contracts. Mighty AI built a premium product in a market racing to the bottom.

records.name: Narrative Science
records.failure_reason: Niche Market & GPT Disruption
records.investors: Sapphire Ventures, Jump Capital, Battery Ventures, In-Q-Tel
records.lesson: Narrative Science spent 12 years building proprietary NLG technology. Then GPT made natural language generation a commodity capability anyone could access through an API.

records.name: Anodot
records.failure_reason: Niche Market & Cloud Platform Competition
records.investors: Aleph, Samsung NEXT, Intel Capital, Redline Capital
records.lesson: AI anomaly detection is a valuable feature but not a company-defining product. Anodot built impressive technology that cloud monitoring platforms absorbed as just another capability.

records.name: C3.ai
records.failure_reason: Slow Growth, Stock Collapse & Customer Concentration
records.investors: Public markets (IPO), Baker Hughes, TPG, Breakthrough Energy
records.lesson: C3.ai is what happens when enterprise AI promises outpace enterprise adoption. Despite a billionaire founder and a $10B IPO valuation, revenue barely grew while the stock lost 85%+.

records.name: Determined AI
records.failure_reason: Open-Source Competition & Cloud Platform Bundling
records.lesson: ML training infrastructure was a crowded space where cloud platforms and open-source tools squeezed out standalone vendors. Even Google Ventures and Sequoia couldn't save a product without a moat.

records.name: Clover Health
records.failure_reason: SPAC Fraud Allegations & Unsustainable Losses
records.investors: Public markets (SPAC via Chamath), Sequoia Capital, First Round Capital, Greenoaks Capital
records.lesson: Chamath Palihapitiya's SPAC empire promised to democratize investing. Clover Health proved it mostly democratized losses — the stock dropped 95% while short sellers exposed undisclosed DOJ investigations.

records.name: Nurx
records.failure_reason: Regulatory Issues & Unsustainable Unit Economics
records.investors: Union Square Ventures, Kleiner Perkins, Y Combinator
records.lesson: Telehealth for birth control prescriptions seemed like a perfect digital health use case. But pharmacy fulfillment costs, regulatory complexity, and insurance billing challenges made every prescription unprofitable.

records.name: Practice Fusion
records.failure_reason: DOJ Kickback Fraud & Failed Business Model
records.investors: Kleiner Perkins, Peter Thiel, Founders Fund, Salesforce Ventures
records.lesson: Free EHR software monetized by pharmaceutical advertising created a fatal conflict of interest. Practice Fusion's CEO went to prison for taking pharma kickbacks that influenced prescribing decisions.

records.name: Wheel Health
records.failure_reason: Post-COVID Telehealth Collapse
records.investors: Tiger Global, Lightspeed, CRV, Silverton Partners
records.lesson: Wheel built telehealth infrastructure for the COVID era. When the pandemic ended and telehealth demand normalized, the company's growth thesis evaporated along with its customers' volumes.

records.name: Zuora
records.failure_reason: Slow Growth & Failed IPO Promise
records.investors: Public markets (IPO), Benchmark, Redpoint, Tenaya Capital, Greylock
records.lesson: Zuora coined 'The Subscription Economy' and built the billing infrastructure for it. But subscription billing turned out to be a feature, not a platform — and Zuora's stock lost 85%+ proving it.

records.name: Domo
records.failure_reason: Overfunding, Slow Growth & BI Market Shift
records.investors: Public markets (IPO), Benchmark, Greylock, IVP, Jeff Bezos
records.lesson: Domo raised nearly $700M to build a BI platform and still couldn't compete with Tableau, Looker, or Power BI. Sometimes the most well-funded company in a category still loses.

records.name: Sumo Logic
records.failure_reason: Lost to Datadog & Cloud Platform Bundling
records.investors: Public markets (IPO), Greylock, Sutter Hill, DFJ, Battery Ventures
records.lesson: Sumo Logic was an early cloud-native log analytics pioneer. But Datadog executed better, cloud providers bundled observability, and Sumo Logic was taken private at a fraction of its peak valuation.

records.name: Fastly
records.failure_reason: Customer Concentration, TikTok Dependency & CDN Commoditization
records.investors: Public markets (IPO), August Capital, Iconiq, IDG Capital
records.lesson: Fastly was the 'developer-friendly CDN' that rode TikTok's growth to a $10B market cap. When TikTok optimized its CDN spend, Fastly lost its largest customer and 85% of its stock value.

records.name: Cloudera
records.failure_reason: Hadoop Obsolescence & Cloud Data Platform Shift
records.investors: Public markets (IPO), Intel Capital, Accel, Greylock, T. Rowe Price
records.lesson: Cloudera bet everything on Hadoop — the technology that was supposed to revolutionize big data. When the world moved to cloud data platforms and Hadoop became legacy, Cloudera's $5B valuation crumbled.

records.name: Apttus
records.failure_reason: Overfunding, Complex Product & CRM Platform Dependency
records.investors: K1 Investment Management, IBM, Salesforce Ventures, Goldman Sachs
records.lesson: Apttus raised $400M+ to build a Configure-Price-Quote platform that lived on top of Salesforce. When Salesforce built its own CPQ, Apttus lost its biggest distribution channel and its strategic moat.

records.name: Radius Intelligence
records.failure_reason: B2B Data Became Commoditized
records.investors: American Express Ventures, Georgian Partners, Founders Fund
records.lesson: Radius built a B2B data platform for sales intelligence. But ZoomInfo, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, and dozens of competitors commoditized B2B data, making Radius's standalone data product uncompetitive.

records.name: Sprinklr
records.failure_reason: Complex Enterprise Sales & Stock Decline
records.investors: Public markets (IPO), Battery Ventures, ICONIQ, Hellman & Friedman, Temasek
records.lesson: Sprinklr built the most comprehensive social media management platform in the world. But 'comprehensive' meant 'complex,' and most customers wanted simple tools, not a $500K/year enterprise platform.

records.name: Glossier
records.failure_reason: DTC Model Collapse & Retail Pivot Too Late
records.investors: Sequoia Capital, IVP, Forerunner Ventures, Index Ventures
records.lesson: DTC-only brands face existential risk when customer acquisition costs rise and wholesale channels are ignored too long.

records.name: Casper (Post-IPO)
records.failure_reason: Unsustainable Unit Economics & Commoditized Product
records.lesson: Venture-scaling a commodity product with thin margins and high return rates creates a race to the bottom that no amount of branding can win.

records.name: Boxed
records.failure_reason: SPAC Implosion & Failed Costco Challenger Model
records.lesson: Challenging entrenched wholesale giants requires massive scale advantages that most startups cannot achieve, especially through SPAC shortcuts.

records.name: Allbirds (Post-IPO)
records.failure_reason: DTC Shoe Brand Failed to Scale Beyond Niche
records.investors: Tiger Global, T. Rowe Price, Franklin Templeton
records.lesson: Sustainability-focused DTC brands face brutal economics when they can't expand beyond their initial audience and face competition from incumbent brands adopting similar messaging.

records.name: Jet.com
records.failure_reason: Failed Amazon Challenger Absorbed & Shut Down
records.investors: Bain Capital, Fidelity, Goldman Sachs, GV
records.lesson: Even $3.3B acquisitions can't save a business model that can't differentiate from the dominant marketplace.

records.name: Groupon
records.failure_reason: Daily Deals Model Proved Unsustainable for Merchants
records.investors: New Enterprise Associates, Accel Partners, Greylock, Battery Ventures
records.lesson: Business models that primarily attract deal-seekers who never become loyal customers create a death spiral for merchant partners and the platform itself.

records.name: Farmstead
records.failure_reason: Online Grocery Margins Too Thin to Build Standalone Business
records.investors: Y Combinator, Forerunner Ventures, Moment Ventures
records.lesson: Online grocery delivery has the thinnest margins in e-commerce — even well-run startups can't compete with incumbents' existing infrastructure.

records.name: Deliveroo
records.failure_reason: Chronic Unprofitability Despite Massive Scale
records.investors: Amazon, T. Rowe Price, Fidelity, Greenoaks Capital
records.lesson: Even with $1.7B in funding and Amazon's backing, food delivery platforms struggle to achieve sustainable profitability due to structural margin challenges.

records.name: Getir (Detailed)
records.failure_reason: Instant Grocery Delivery Model Burned Through $5.5B
records.investors: Sequoia Capital, Tiger Global, Mubadala, Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth
records.lesson: Instant grocery delivery requires such massive subsidies per order that even $5.5B in funding can't bridge the gap to profitability.

records.name: Jokr
records.failure_reason: Burned $430M in 2 Years on Failed Quick Commerce
records.investors: GGV Capital, Tiger Global, Balderton Capital
records.lesson: Launching an instant delivery startup after the model was already failing for others is peak VC FOMO — the failure was predictable before the first dark store opened.

records.name: Didi (DiDi Global)
records.failure_reason: Regulatory Crackdown After Controversial US IPO
records.lesson: Going public in the US against your home government's wishes can trigger an existential regulatory response that no amount of funding can overcome.

records.name: Getaround
records.failure_reason: Peer-to-Peer Car Sharing Never Achieved Profitability
records.lesson: Peer-to-peer car sharing has structural challenges — supply quality is inconsistent, utilization rates are low, and the model can't compete with professional fleet operators on reliability.

records.name: Zum
records.failure_reason: School Transportation Tech Faced Razor-Thin Public Sector Margins
records.investors: SoftBank Vision Fund, GGV Capital, BMW i Ventures
records.lesson: Modernizing public sector services (school buses) sounds transformative but faces procurement bureaucracy, budget constraints, and razor-thin margins that don't support venture returns.

records.name: Grab Holdings
records.failure_reason: Southeast Asia's Super-App Struggles to Reach Profitability
records.lesson: Building a super-app across fragmented Southeast Asian markets with ride-hailing, delivery, and fintech requires massive capital and patience — profitability may take a decade or more.

records.name: Better.com
records.failure_reason: Toxic CEO Culture & Market Timing Disaster
records.investors: SoftBank, Activant Capital, Goldman Sachs, L Catterton
records.lesson: A toxic founder who fires 900 employees via Zoom can destroy a billion-dollar company even when the underlying product has genuine value.

records.name: Clubhouse (Social Audio)
records.failure_reason: Audio-Only Social Network Was a Pandemic Fad
records.investors: Andreessen Horowitz, DST Global, Tiger Global
records.lesson: Products that thrive in pandemic lockdown conditions may have zero product-market fit in the real world where people have alternatives to sitting in audio rooms.

records.name: Tumblr (Yahoo Acquisition)
records.failure_reason: $1.1B Acquisition Wrote Down to $3M — 99.7% Value Destruction
records.investors: Yahoo (acquired for $1.1B), Union Square Ventures, Spark Capital
records.lesson: Acquiring a social platform for $1.1B without a monetization plan, then banning the content that drives engagement, is a masterclass in value destruction.

records.name: SolarCity (Tesla Acquisition)
records.failure_reason: Unsustainable economics & bailout acquisition
records.lesson: Customer acquisition costs exceeded lifetime value in residential solar, requiring Tesla bailout that destroyed $2B+ in shareholder value.

records.name: Bloom Energy
records.failure_reason: Chronic unprofitability & accounting issues
records.lesson: Two decades of losses despite $1.7B in funding proved that fuel cell technology couldn't achieve cost competitiveness with cheaper alternatives.

records.name: SunEdison
records.failure_reason: Massive debt-fueled acquisition spree
records.lesson: The largest renewable energy bankruptcy in history ($16.1B in debts) was caused by reckless acquisitions financed with unsustainable debt structures.

records.name: Lordstown Motors (Detailed)
records.failure_reason: Fake pre-orders & failed production
records.lesson: SPAC-listed EV startup collapsed after SEC investigation revealed fake pre-orders and the company failed to deliver a viable product.

records.name: Quanergy Systems
records.failure_reason: Failed to deliver solid-state LiDAR
records.lesson: Promised revolutionary solid-state LiDAR at $100/unit but never delivered a competitive product as the market was flooded with cheaper alternatives.

records.name: Desktop Metal
records.failure_reason: Revenue never matched valuation
records.lesson: Despite $800M raised and a $6.3B peak valuation, Desktop Metal never achieved profitability in metal 3D printing as adoption remained niche.

records.name: Rethink Robotics (Detailed)
records.failure_reason: Product didn't meet industrial needs
records.lesson: Pioneer of collaborative robots failed because Baxter was too slow and imprecise for real manufacturing, while cheaper and better alternatives emerged.

records.name: SoftBank Robotics (Pepper)
records.failure_reason: No clear use case for humanoid robot
records.lesson: Despite $2B+ investment, Pepper the humanoid robot never found a sustainable use case as businesses couldn't justify the cost for a glorified greeter.

records.name: Starship Technologies
records.failure_reason: Unit economics didn't scale
records.lesson: Sidewalk delivery robots were a technical marvel but couldn't achieve cost-effectiveness versus human delivery at scale outside of campus environments.

records.name: SoFi Technologies
records.failure_reason: Student loan moratorium & competition
records.lesson: SoFi's core student loan refinancing business was destroyed by the federal student loan moratorium while its pivot to becoming a full bank faced intense competition.

records.name: Luma (Camera Hardware)
records.failure_reason: Smart home camera in overcrowded market
records.lesson: Attempted to build premium smart home camera competing against Amazon, Google, and Netgear with insufficient scale and brand recognition.

records.name: Kuri (Mayfield Robotics)
records.failure_reason: No compelling use case for home robot
records.lesson: Bosch-backed home robot was adorable but useless — couldn't justify $799 price when it did less than a $50 smart speaker.

records.name: Electric Last Mile Solutions (Detailed)
records.failure_reason: Insider trading & failed product
records.lesson: SPAC-listed EV delivery van company collapsed in under 2 years after SEC investigation revealed executives bought shares before the SPAC deal was announced.

records.name: Velodyne Lidar
records.failure_reason: Pioneer overtaken by cheaper competitors
records.lesson: The company that invented modern LiDAR for autonomous vehicles was overtaken by cheaper competitors and sold for just $4.40/share after peaking at $24.

records.name: Karma Automotive
records.failure_reason: Luxury EV with no market
records.lesson: The successor to Fisker Automotive burned through $1B+ trying to sell luxury plug-in hybrids that nobody wanted, producing fewer than 3,000 cars in a decade.

records.name: Body Labs
records.failure_reason: B2B 3D body scanning market too small
records.lesson: Pioneering 3D body scanning technology from Brown University couldn't find enough paying customers in fashion/fitness to sustain operations.

records.name: Carbon Robotics
records.failure_reason: Hardware costs exceeded farmer ROI
records.lesson: AI-powered laser weeding robots were technically impressive but too expensive for most farmers, with each unit costing $1M+ and requiring specialized operation.

records.name: ecobee
records.failure_reason: Couldn't compete with Google/Amazon smart home
records.lesson: Canadian smart thermostat pioneer raised $200M but couldn't compete against Nest (Google) and Amazon in the smart home ecosystem war.

records.name: Impossible Aerospace
records.failure_reason: Battery-centric drone design couldn't compete
records.lesson: Ex-Tesla engineer's 'flying battery' drone concept couldn't achieve price-performance parity with established drone makers DJI and Skydio.

records.name: Plastc Card
records.failure_reason: Failed to ship smart card product
records.lesson: Collected $9M in pre-orders for a smart credit card that could store multiple cards, but never shipped the product as Apple Pay and Google Wallet made it obsolete.

records.name: Essential Products (Detailed)
records.failure_reason: Android founder couldn't compete with Apple/Samsung
records.lesson: Even Andy Rubin (Android creator) couldn't build a competitive smartphone brand, as the Essential Phone sold fewer than 150K units despite massive hype.

records.name: Zume Pizza (Detailed)
records.failure_reason: Robot pizza was a solution looking for a problem
records.lesson: SoftBank poured $375M into robot-made pizza, then the company pivoted to compostable packaging before collapsing — a textbook case of technology in search of a market.

records.name: Lilium (Detailed)
records.failure_reason: eVTOL physics don't work economically
records.lesson: European air taxi startup burned $1.5B developing an electric vertical takeoff jet that couldn't achieve the range, speed, or cost targets needed for commercial viability.

records.name: ICON (3D-Printed Homes)
records.failure_reason: 3D-printed homes not cheaper than traditional
records.lesson: Despite $451M raised and massive media hype, 3D-printed homes couldn't achieve cost savings over traditional construction when factoring in land, permits, plumbing, and electrical.

records.name: Peloton (Detailed Decline)
records.failure_reason: COVID boom was temporary, not permanent
records.lesson: Peloton mistook pandemic-driven demand for permanent market shift, expanded manufacturing capacity just as gyms reopened and demand collapsed 80%.

records.name: TripAdvisor (Decline)
records.failure_reason: Google dominance & shifting travel behavior
records.lesson: TripAdvisor's review empire crumbled as Google integrated reviews directly into search, eliminating the need for a separate review destination.

records.name: Getaway House
records.failure_reason: Overexpansion & thin margins in cabin rental
records.lesson: Getaway expanded to 15+ outposts chasing growth but discovered that building and maintaining remote cabins had razor-thin margins that couldn't support venture-scale returns.

records.name: Sonder Holdings
records.failure_reason: Cash burn & unsustainable lease commitments
records.lesson: Sonder leased apartments and operated them as hotels, but the model required massive upfront investment in each unit while generating hotel-like margins — the worst of both worlds.

records.name: Kiwi.com
records.failure_reason: Virtual interlining model collapse & airline pushback
records.lesson: Kiwi.com's innovation of combining flights from different airlines fell apart when airlines blocked screen scraping and refused to honor connecting itineraries they didn't sell.

records.name: Flyr
records.failure_reason: Overambitious airline SaaS pivot & cash burn
records.lesson: Flyr pivoted from consumer fare prediction to enterprise airline revenue management SaaS, but the sales cycles were 18-24 months and airline customers were notoriously slow adopters.

records.name: Atrium (Legal Tech)
records.failure_reason: Technology couldn't replace lawyer judgment
records.lesson: Justin Kan's attempt to build a tech-enabled law firm discovered that legal work's complexity makes it resistant to the automation and scaling that works in software.

records.name: Luminance
records.failure_reason: AI overpromise & slow legal enterprise sales
records.lesson: Luminance promised AI-powered contract review would replace junior lawyers, but law firms discovered the technology required more human oversight than advertised, limiting ROI.

records.name: DoNotPay
records.failure_reason: Legal accuracy failures & unauthorized practice claims
records.lesson: DoNotPay marketed itself as a 'robot lawyer' but was accused of providing inaccurate legal information that could harm consumers, and faced unauthorized practice of law complaints.

records.name: Clio (Growth Challenges)
records.failure_reason: Overfunding & LLM disruption threat to premium pricing
records.lesson: Clio raised nearly $1B for legal practice management software but faces existential pressure as AI-powered alternatives threaten its premium pricing model.

records.name: Notarize
records.failure_reason: Post-COVID demand collapse & regulatory fragmentation
records.lesson: Notarize exploded during COVID when remote notarization became essential, but demand collapsed as in-person services resumed and state-by-state regulations limited growth.

records.name: Lemonade (Detailed)
records.failure_reason: Unsustainable loss ratios & failed AI underwriting
records.lesson: Lemonade promised AI would revolutionize insurance underwriting, but its loss ratios remained above 90% — far worse than traditional insurers — proving that technology alone can't fix insurance economics.

records.name: Hippo Insurance
records.failure_reason: Catastrophic loss ratios & climate risk underpricing
records.lesson: Hippo's home insurance model dramatically underpriced climate risk, leading to 166% loss ratios during wildfire and hurricane seasons that wiped out years of premium income.

records.name: Metromile (Detailed)
records.failure_reason: Per-mile pricing attracted wrong customer base
records.lesson: Metromile's pay-per-mile car insurance attracted low-mileage drivers who also happened to be the lowest-risk, lowest-premium customers — the ones traditional insurers wanted most.

records.name: Root Insurance (Detailed)
records.failure_reason: Telematics data didn't improve underwriting profitably
records.lesson: Root raised $1.2B betting that smartphone telematics would revolutionize car insurance pricing, but the data wasn't predictive enough to beat traditional actuarial models at scale.

records.name: wefox (Detailed)
records.failure_reason: Governance scandals & unsustainable growth at any cost
records.lesson: Europe's most-funded insurtech raised $1.6B but faced allegations of inflated metrics, governance failures, and loss ratios that proved the business was buying revenue at unsustainable costs.

records.name: Vine (Detailed)
records.failure_reason: Twitter neglect & Instagram/Snapchat competition
records.lesson: Vine invented short-form video but Twitter failed to invest in creator monetization, allowing Instagram and Snapchat to poach Vine's top creators by offering money and better tools.

records.name: Parler
records.failure_reason: Platform deplatforming & content moderation failure
records.lesson: Parler positioned itself as a free-speech alternative to Twitter but discovered that platform infrastructure providers (AWS, Apple, Google) have their own content policies that override your business model.

records.name: Friendster
records.failure_reason: Technical failures & Facebook competition
records.lesson: Friendster was the original social network but suffered from chronic site performance issues (20+ second load times) that drove users to MySpace and then Facebook.

records.name: Ello
records.failure_reason: No business model beyond anti-advertising manifesto
records.lesson: Ello attracted millions of users who hated Facebook's ads, but discovered that an ad-free social network with no subscription revenue has no way to sustain itself.

records.name: Path
records.failure_reason: 150-friend limit & failed monetization
records.lesson: Path's intentional 150-friend cap created intimate social sharing but severely limited growth potential and network effects, making it impossible to compete with Facebook's expanding ecosystem.

records.name: Google+
records.failure_reason: Forced adoption & no differentiation from Facebook
records.lesson: Even Google's massive resources and distribution (forcing G+ onto YouTube, Gmail, Android) couldn't create a social network that users actually wanted to use.

records.name: Oscar Health
records.failure_reason: Healthcare costs outpaced tech savings
records.lesson: Oscar raised $1.6B to make health insurance user-friendly with a consumer tech approach, but discovered that great UX can't fix the fundamental problem of rising healthcare costs.

records.name: Mastodon
records.failure_reason: Complexity barrier & post-Twitter hype collapse
records.lesson: Mastodon's decentralized architecture appealed to idealists but confused mainstream users. Server selection, federation rules, and content fragmentation created friction that prevented mass adoption.

records.name: Honest Policy / PolicyGenius Struggles
records.failure_reason: Insurance comparison margins too thin for VC returns
records.lesson: Insurance comparison platforms generate leads but can't capture enough value in the transaction. Insurers pay $20-50 per lead while it costs $100+ in digital advertising to acquire each shopper.

records.name: Take Eat Easy
records.failure_reason: Brussels-founded (later Paris-headquartered) food-delivery startup Take Eat Easy, launched in 2012 by siblings Adrien and Chloé Roose with Karim Slaoui, ceased trading on 26 Jul 2016 — the same week it announced its 1-millionth delivery. After raising €16M and expanding to Paris, London, Madrid and Berlin, Take Eat Easy failed to close a Series C round it needed to compete with Deliveroo and UberEats, and filed for juridical reorganisation. It was one of the first high-profile 2010s food-delivery casualties in Europe.
records.investors: Rocket Internet, DN Capital, Piton Capital
records.lesson: Belgian-French food-delivery pioneer ran out of cash before reaching scale. The Series B that didn't close became one of Europe's most-cited startup failure post-mortems.

records.name: Cityscoot (Insolvency)
records.failure_reason: Paris-based free-floating electric scooter service Cityscoot, founded 2014 by Bertrand Fleurose, raised €70M+ from RATP, Allianz and BPI France to run one of Europe's largest shared-moped fleets. After the free-floating micromobility crash of 2022-23, Cityscoot entered insolvency proceedings at the Paris commercial court. On 21 Feb 2024 the court accepted Spanish competitor Cooltra's takeover bid for just €400k — retaining only 30 of 157-168 employees and effectively wiping shareholders.
records.lesson: Paris electric-scooter-sharing pioneer Cityscoot raised €60M from RATP and Allianz then filed for liquidation in 2024 — France's defining shared-mobility failure.

records.name: Luko
records.failure_reason: Paris-based home-insurance startup Luko, founded 2016 by Raphaël Vullierme and Benoît Bourdel, raised €65M and was valued at €250M in late 2020. After failing to reach profitability, Luko announced an acquisition by UK insurer Admiral in Oct 2023 for €14M — a deal Admiral pulled after audits in Nov 2023. Luko was placed in receivership in Dec 2023 and finally acquired by Allianz Direct on 25 Jan 2024 for just €4.3M (~$4.65M) at the Paris commercial court, wiping out shareholders.
records.investors: EQT Ventures, Founders Fund, Speedinvest, Accel, Xavier Niel
records.lesson: Paris home-insurance unicorn-aspirant Luko was acquired by Allianz Direct subsidiary Admiral in 2023 at a steep discount, then its German subsidiary entered insolvency.

records.name: Habx (Acquired in Distress)
records.failure_reason: French Property Market Collapse
records.lesson: Paris PropTech Habx raised €40M to digitalize new-build property pre-sales then filed for insolvency in 2024 as the French property market collapsed.

records.name: Ÿnsect
records.failure_reason: French insect-protein pioneer Ÿnsect (founded 2011) raised over €600M — the largest agtech funding round outside the US — to build the world's largest vertical insect farm at Amiens for pet food and aquaculture feed. The Amiens facility ran years behind schedule with severe cost overruns. In Jul 2025 Ÿnsect took an €8.6M emergency bridge from historical investors alongside mass layoffs. A commercial court placed the company in supervised restructuring and extended the observation period to 12 Jan 2026. TechCrunch's Dec 2025 investigation described 'how reality crushed Ÿnsect'.
records.investors: Astanor, Robert Downey Jr's FootPrint Coalition, Upfront Ventures
records.lesson: France's most-funded AgTech, insect-protein producer Ÿnsect, raised $625M then entered French safeguard proceedings in 2024 as capital-intensive scaling proved unviable.

records.name: Tilkee (Acquired Distress)
records.failure_reason: Failed to Scale Internationally
records.lesson: Lyon B2B SaaS Tilkee raised €8M from Bpifrance then was acquired in distress in 2023 — a representative case for French SMB SaaS unable to scale beyond France.

records.name: Cazoo France (Market Exit)
records.failure_reason: Pan-European Retreat
records.lesson: UK used-car unicorn Cazoo entered France in 2021 with massive marketing then withdrew entirely from France, Italy, Spain and Germany in 2023 — wiping out hundreds of millions in continental investment.

records.name: Withings (Nokia Acquisition Crisis)
records.failure_reason: Nokia Write-Down & Failed Integration
records.lesson: Paris connected-health pioneer Withings was acquired by Nokia for €170M in 2016, then written down to near-zero by 2017 — Nokia eventually sold it back to its founder for a symbolic price. A canonical French acqui-failure.

records.name: ManoMano (Massive Down Round)
records.failure_reason: Post-COVID Demand & Profitability Push
records.investors: General Atlantic, Eurazeo, Bpifrance, Aglaé Ventures
records.lesson: Paris DIY-marketplace unicorn ManoMano raised $725M then conducted multiple rounds of layoffs and reportedly accepted a steep down-round in 2024 as post-COVID DIY demand collapsed.

records.name: Ledger (Crypto-Winter Down Round)
records.failure_reason: Crypto Winter & Markdown
records.investors: 10T Holdings, Cathay Innovation, Digital Currency Group
records.lesson: Paris crypto-hardware unicorn Ledger reached $1.5B valuation in 2021, then conducted layoffs and reportedly accepted significant valuation markdowns through 2023-2024.

records.name: Sorare (Markdown)
records.failure_reason: NFT Crash & Volume Collapse
records.investors: SoftBank Vision Fund, Atomico, Benchmark, Accel
records.lesson: Paris fantasy-sports-NFT unicorn Sorare raised $680M from SoftBank at $4.3B in 2021, then reportedly suffered massive valuation markdowns and revenue collapse as the NFT market crashed.

records.name: Believe (Public Markdown)
records.failure_reason: Public-Market Failure & Take-Private
records.lesson: Paris-listed digital-music distributor Believe IPOed at €19.50 in 2021, then was taken private at €15 in 2024 after a value-destructive public-market journey — a major French IPO failure.

records.name: Ornikar (Down Round & Layoffs)
records.failure_reason: Failed International Expansion & Layoffs
records.lesson: Paris driving-school unicorn Ornikar reached $750M valuation in 2021, then conducted significant layoffs and exited Spain in 2023 as international scaling failed.

records.name: Meero (Founder-Driven Crisis)
records.failure_reason: Mass Layoffs & Restructuring
records.investors: Eurazeo, Prime Ventures, Alven, Idinvest, White Star Capital
records.lesson: Paris on-demand-photography unicorn Meero raised $293M at $1B valuation in 2019, then conducted brutal layoffs (80%+ of staff) in 2020-23 — a defining French unicorn meltdown.

records.name: Sono Motors
records.failure_reason: Munich-based Sono Motors listed on NASDAQ in Nov 2021 promising the Sion — a €25,000 partly solar-powered EV backed by 21,000+ pre-orders. On Feb 24 2023 the company cancelled the Sion program and laid off ~75% of staff, pivoting to a B2B solar-integration business. On May 15 2023 Sono Group NV and Sono Motors GmbH filed for self-administration (Eigenverwaltung) under the German Insolvency Act after failing to secure the ~$100M needed to bring the Sion to production.
records.lesson: Munich-based solar-powered car startup Sono Motors raised hundreds of millions including a Nasdaq IPO, but cancelled its consumer Sion vehicle in early 2023 and filed for insolvency three months later.

records.name: Auxmoney (Down Round)
records.failure_reason: Rate Hikes & Default Spike
records.lesson: Düsseldorf-based P2P consumer-lender Auxmoney conducted layoffs and a flat-to-down round as German interest-rate hikes spiked default rates and crushed P2P-lending economics in 2022-23.

records.name: Vay (Berlin Exit)
records.failure_reason: Pivot Away from Berlin Market
records.lesson: Berlin teledriving startup Vay, after raising $110M, exited its German operations in 2024 to focus solely on Las Vegas — leaving its home market and laying off most Berlin staff.

records.name: Coya
records.failure_reason: Acquisition at Steep Discount
records.lesson: Berlin Thiel-backed digital insurer Coya raised $70M+ and was sold to Luko in 2022 at a steep discount, then collapsed entirely with Luko's own insolvency in 2023.

records.name: Kiwigrid
records.failure_reason: Insolvency After Strategic Investor Pullback
records.lesson: Dresden energy-IoT startup Kiwigrid filed insolvency in 2024 after corporate strategic investors LG and E.ON pulled support — a classic German corporate-VC dependency failure.

records.name: VEACT
records.failure_reason: Customer Concentration & Insolvency
records.lesson: Munich automotive-CRM SaaS VEACT filed insolvency in 2023 after over-reliance on a small group of large dealer-group customers — one of the German automotive-tech failures of the year.

records.name: Infarm
records.failure_reason: Berlin-based vertical farming unicorn Infarm, founded by Israeli siblings Erez & Guy Galonska and Osnat Michaeli, raised over $500M and reached $1B+ valuation in Dec 2021. In Nov 2022 the company announced a mass restructuring, closing operations in the UK, France, Netherlands, Spain, Portugal, US and Denmark to focus on 'Growing Centers' in fewer, larger locations. Its Dutch arm was declared bankrupt in 2023, and by Dec 2023 Sifted reported Infarm had 'all but disappeared' — a textbook case of vertical-farming unit economics failing at scale.
records.investors: Atomico, Lightrock, Qatar Investment Authority, Hanaco
records.lesson: Berlin's vertical-farming unicorn raised $600M to grow herbs in supermarkets across Europe, then exited every European market in 2023 as the energy crisis destroyed already-thin unit economics.

records.name: Forto (Down Round & Layoffs)
records.failure_reason: Freight Rate Collapse & Layoffs
records.investors: SoftBank Vision Fund, Citi Ventures, Maersk
records.lesson: Berlin digital-freight unicorn Forto raised $590M from SoftBank then conducted multiple layoff rounds and a reported steep down-round as ocean freight rates normalized in 2023.

records.name: Flink (Down Round & Retreat)
records.failure_reason: Berlin quick-commerce startup Flink hit a $5B valuation at the peak of the 2022 speedy-grocery bubble, then watched its category collapse — Gorillas was acquired by Getir, Getir itself exited the US/UK/Europe, and Gopuff retreated. In Sep 2024 Flink raised $150M ($115M equity + $35M debt) from Mubadala, Bond, Northzone and REWE at a valuation of just under $1B — an ~80% down round. Flink is now one of Europe's last surviving speedy-grocery players but the equity story of 2021 is fully unwound.
records.investors: Mubadala, Prosus, BOND, REWE Group, DoorDash
records.lesson: Berlin quick-commerce challenger Flink raised $1.1B at $5B valuation, then exited France in 2023 and accepted a steep down-round in 2024 as the entire q-commerce category collapsed.

records.name: Solaris SE Crisis
records.failure_reason: Berlin banking-as-a-service pioneer Solaris SE (formerly Solarisbank) reached a €1.6B valuation in 2022 as European fintechs raced to embed banking. In March 2024 BaFin fined the company €6.5M for systematically late suspicious-activity reports — a record fine that highlighted compliance failures. Solaris raised a €96M Series F in March 2024 to stabilise, then agreed in Dec 2024 / Jan 2025 to sell a >70% majority stake to Japan's SBI Holdings for ~€100M in a round that slashed the valuation to a fraction of its 2022 peak.
records.investors: SBI Group, BBVA, ABN AMRO, Vulcan Capital, Lakestar
records.lesson: Berlin BaaS unicorn Solaris faced BaFin regulatory restrictions, multiple rounds of layoffs, and a 2024 rescue round at a sharp down valuation — the largest German BaaS crisis to date.

records.name: Snapdeal
records.failure_reason: Intense Competition & Cash Burn
records.lesson: Snapdeal was once India's #1 e-commerce platform but lost to Flipkart and Amazon India by trying to be everything at once instead of finding a defensible niche.

records.name: Housing.com
records.failure_reason: Founder Misconduct & Cash Burn
records.investors: SoftBank, Falcon Edge, Helion Ventures, Nexus Venture Partners
records.lesson: A brilliant product cannot survive a toxic founder. Rahul Yadav's public feuds with investors led to his firing and the company's decline.

records.name: Hike Messenger
records.failure_reason: WhatsApp Dominance & Constant Pivots
records.lesson: India's WhatsApp killer never found product-market fit despite $261M in funding. Constant pivots — messaging to social to content to crypto — signaled a lack of clear vision.

records.name: Koo
records.failure_reason: User Retention & Monetization Failure
records.investors: Tiger Global, Accel, 3one4 Capital, Blume Ventures
records.lesson: Being the 'Indian Twitter' with government support wasn't enough. Without organic user engagement and a monetization model, Koo couldn't survive.

records.name: Lido Learning
records.failure_reason: Post-COVID Demand Collapse & Cash Burn
records.lesson: Lido expanded from 300 to 1,200 employees during COVID but couldn't sustain growth when schools reopened. The company shut down overnight, leaving employees without their last salary.

records.name: Vedantu
records.failure_reason: Post-COVID Demand Decline & Cash Burn
records.investors: Tiger Global, Coatue, GGV Capital, WestBridge
records.lesson: Vedantu achieved unicorn status during COVID but laid off 40% of staff in 2022. The live tutoring model was too expensive for India's price-sensitive parents.

records.name: ShopClues
records.failure_reason: Founder Disputes & Competition
records.investors: Tiger Global, Nexus Venture Partners, GIC
records.lesson: ShopClues reached unicorn status targeting Tier 2-3 India but collapsed due to founder disputes and inability to compete with Flipkart/Amazon.

records.name: PepperTap
records.failure_reason: Unsustainable Unit Economics
records.lesson: India's hyperlocal grocery delivery economics didn't work in 2015. PepperTap spent ₹300 to deliver a ₹150 order. It was 8 years too early for quick commerce.

records.name: TinyOwl
records.failure_reason: Mismanagement & Premature Scaling
records.investors: Matrix Partners, Sequoia India, Nexus Venture Partners
records.lesson: TinyOwl expanded from 1 to 11 cities, then retreated to 1. Employees held the founder hostage when layoffs were announced without severance. A cautionary tale of startup chaos.

records.name: Paytm Mall
records.failure_reason: Cashback Fraud & Strategic Confusion
records.lesson: Paytm Mall's O2O (online-to-offline) model confused merchants and customers. Rampant cashback fraud by sellers inflated GMV artificially.

records.name: BharatPe
records.failure_reason: Governance Crisis & Founder Scandal
records.investors: Tiger Global, Sequoia India, Coatue, Dragoneer
records.lesson: BharatPe's co-founder Ashneer Grover became famous on Shark Tank India but was ousted over alleged financial fraud. The company survived but was severely damaged.

records.name: Zilingo
records.failure_reason: Accounting Fraud & Governance Failure
records.lesson: Zilingo's Indian-origin CEO was suspended for alleged accounting irregularities. The Sequoia-backed fashion platform was liquidated after a forensic audit revealed revenue inflation.

records.name: FreshMenu
records.failure_reason: Cloud Kitchen Economics & Competition
records.lesson: FreshMenu built cloud kitchens before it was trendy but couldn't compete with Swiggy and Zomato's aggregation model. Vertical integration in food delivery is capital-intensive.

records.name: Udaan
records.failure_reason: Cash Burn & B2B Marketplace Challenges
records.investors: DST Global, Lightspeed, GGV Capital, Altimeter, Microsoft
records.lesson: Udaan became the fastest Indian unicorn but discovered that digitizing India's fragmented B2B trade required enormous capital and patience.

records.name: CommonFloor
records.failure_reason: Competition & Market Timing
records.lesson: CommonFloor was acquired and shut down by Quikr. Despite innovation (3D property tours, community features), it couldn't build a sustainable business in India's fractured real estate market.

records.name: Rivigo
records.failure_reason: Capital-Intensive Model & Market Challenges
records.investors: Warburg Pincus, SAIF Partners, Spring Capital
records.lesson: Rivigo tried to revolutionize Indian trucking with relay-based logistics but the asset-heavy model burned through $325M without achieving profitability.

records.name: Portea Medical
records.failure_reason: Unit Economics & Scaling Challenges
records.investors: Accel, Qualcomm Ventures, Sabre Partners, IFC
records.lesson: Home healthcare in India sounds perfect on paper but Portea discovered that managing thousands of healthcare workers across cities with razor-thin margins is incredibly difficult.

records.name: CureFit (Cult.fit)
records.failure_reason: Over-Diversification & COVID Impact
records.lesson: CureFit tried to be everything — gym, food, mental health, primary care — at once. The 'super app for health' vision required infinite capital in a price-sensitive market.

records.name: Bounce
records.failure_reason: Asset-Heavy Model & EV Pivot Failure
records.investors: Accel, B Capital, Falcon Edge, Chiratae
records.lesson: Bounce went from scooter rentals to EV manufacturing and back, burning $220M in pivots. The company couldn't decide if it was a rental service or a vehicle manufacturer.

records.name: WhiteHat Jr
records.failure_reason: Misleading Marketing & Post-Acquisition Write-Down
records.investors: Byju's (acquirer), Owl Ventures, Nexus Venture Partners
records.lesson: WhiteHat Jr's aggressive marketing — featuring fake student success stories and dubious coding claims for 6-year-olds — made it a poster child for EdTech hype. Acquired by Byju's for $300M, it was later written down to near zero.

records.name: Dazo
records.failure_reason: Unit Economics & Market Timing
records.lesson: Dazo tried to deliver home-cooked meals from households but the model couldn't ensure quality, hygiene, or consistency at scale.

records.name: Unacademy
records.failure_reason: Excessive Acquisitions & Post-COVID Decline
records.investors: SoftBank, Tiger Global, General Atlantic, Sequoia India
records.lesson: Unacademy made 10 acquisitions including PrepLadder ($50M), CodeChef, and Relevel but couldn't integrate them. When EdTech demand fell, the conglomerate structure bled cash from every direction.

records.name: Meesho (Challenges)
records.failure_reason: Profitability Struggles & Model Pivots
records.investors: SoftBank, Prosus, Meta, B Capital, Sequoia India
records.lesson: Meesho pivoted from social commerce to zero-commission marketplace, capturing massive volumes but with razor-thin margins. Profitability remained elusive despite 150M+ transacting users.

records.name: Vogo
records.failure_reason: COVID Impact & Asset-Heavy Model
records.lesson: Vogo's scooter rental business was devastated by COVID. Maintaining 10,000+ scooters across cities required massive capital that dried up when shared mobility demand collapsed.

records.name: Stayzilla
records.failure_reason: Competition & Founder Arrest
records.lesson: Stayzilla was one of India's oldest startups. Its founder was arrested over a vendor payment dispute after shutdown — highlighting the legal risks of startup failures in India.

records.name: Grofers (pre-Blinkit)
records.failure_reason: Model Failure & Forced Pivot
records.lesson: Grofers' original same-day grocery delivery model failed. Only after pivoting to 10-minute delivery (Blinkit) and selling to Zomato for $568M did it find a sustainable path — but as a different company entirely.

records.name: Fabelio
records.failure_reason: Cash Burn & Failed Funding Round
records.lesson: Indonesia's Wayfair-style furniture e-commerce raised US$30M then declared bankruptcy in 2022 after failing to secure a Series C.

records.name: TaniHub
records.failure_reason: Pivot Fatigue & Layoffs
records.investors: MDI Ventures, BRI Ventures, Openspace Ventures, Intudo Ventures
records.lesson: Indonesia's flagship AgTech raised US$110M then conducted multiple rounds of layoffs as commodity-margin AgTech proved harder than projected.

records.name: Pluang (Down Round)
records.failure_reason: Crypto Winter & Path to Profit
records.lesson: Indonesia's wealth-app Pluang raised US$160M during the crypto boom then conducted layoffs and reportedly accepted a flat-to-down round.

records.name: Ula
records.failure_reason: Capital-Intensive Inventory Model
records.investors: Tiger Global, Bezos Expeditions, Sequoia India, Lightspeed
records.lesson: Tiger-Global-and-Bezos-backed Ula raised US$140M then shut down its core B2B Indonesia operations in 2023 — a major regional B2B e-commerce failure.

records.name: Sirclo (Layoffs)
records.failure_reason: Post-COVID Demand & Profitability Push
records.lesson: Indonesia's Shopify-equivalent Sirclo raised US$130M then conducted significant layoffs and shut acquired brands as Indonesian e-commerce SaaS margins disappointed.

records.name: Halofina (Wind-Down)
records.failure_reason: Failed to Reach Scale
records.lesson: Indonesian financial-planning app Halofina shut down in 2023 — a representative example of smaller Indonesian fintech apps failing to reach scale.

records.name: Mosaicoon
records.failure_reason: Pivot Fatigue & Cash Burn
records.investors: United Ventures, Vertis, Atlante Ventures, Intesa Sanpaolo
records.lesson: Italy's most-hyped video-content startup pivoted three times in five years and ran out of runway before finding scalable revenue.

records.name: Cortilia (Down Round)
records.failure_reason: Failed to Reach Profitability
records.lesson: Milan grocery e-commerce Cortilia raised €20M+ then conducted multiple layoff rounds and a flat-to-down financing in 2023 as Italian grocery-e-commerce demand normalized post-COVID.

records.name: Jobrapido (Symphony Pull)
records.failure_reason: US Parent Strategic Pullback
records.lesson: Milan-founded job-search aggregator Jobrapido was wound down by US parent Symphony in 2023 after years of Italian operations — a defining Italian acqui-failure.

records.name: Hype/Banca Sella Pivot
records.failure_reason: Strategic Failure & Banca Sella Buyback
records.lesson: Italian neobank Hype, after raising €80M+ in a JV with Illimity, was bought back by Banca Sella in 2023 at a discount as the JV failed to reach scale.

records.name: Musement (TUI Write-Down)
records.failure_reason: Acquired & Largely Wound Down
records.lesson: Milan tours-and-experiences platform Musement was acquired by TUI for €60M in 2018, then largely wound down post-COVID in 2023 — destroying most acquisition value.

records.name: MoneyFarm (Flat Round & Layoffs)
records.failure_reason: Failed to Reach Profitability
records.investors: Poste Italiane, M&G, Allianz Asset Management, United Ventures
records.lesson: Italian wealthtech MoneyFarm raised €170M+ then conducted layoffs and reportedly accepted a flat-to-down round in 2023 as European wealthtech profitability remained elusive.

records.name: Velasca (Distress)
records.failure_reason: DTC Footwear Margins
records.lesson: Milan DTC men's-shoe brand Velasca, after raising €15M+, restructured in 2024 amid intense pressure on Italian DTC fashion brands.

records.name: Everli (Supermercato24)
records.failure_reason: Milan grocery-delivery scaleup Everli (formerly Supermercato24) raised $200M+ and was valued at over €450M in 2021, backed by Verlinvest and DN Capital. After failing to raise a follow-on round in 2023, Everli was sold for €1 to Palella Holdings in Feb 2024 through a €21M capital increase — one of the most public down-and-out exits in Italian tech. The company had already exited France, Poland and Czechia and made mass redundancies before the sale.
records.investors: Verlinvest, Luxor Capital, FITEC, DN Capital
records.lesson: Milan grocery-delivery unicorn Everli raised $200M+ then conducted mass layoffs and exited multiple countries in 2023 as European q-commerce collapsed.

records.name: Casavo (Distress & Layoffs)
records.failure_reason: iBuyer Model & Italian Property Slowdown
records.lesson: Milan iBuyer Casavo raised over €400M including from Exor (Agnelli) at a unicorn valuation, then conducted multiple layoff rounds and was reported to be in significant financial distress in 2024.

records.name: Scalapay
records.failure_reason: Milan BNPL unicorn Scalapay raised $808.5M across 5 rounds and hit $1B valuation in Feb 2022 backed by Tencent, Tiger Global and Willoughby Capital. As the global BNPL bubble burst (Klarna's valuation fell 85%, Affirm halved), Scalapay never raised a priced up-round after 2022 and quietly shifted to debt financing — a $81.5M debt facility in Dec 2025 signalled that equity markets had closed. Layoffs and market retrenchment followed as unit economics on 'pay in 3' collapsed under rising rates and defaults.
records.investors: Tencent, Tiger Global, Willoughby Capital, Gangwal, Fasanara
records.lesson: Milan BNPL unicorn Scalapay reached $1B valuation in 2022, then suffered significant reported markdowns and layoffs as the global BNPL sector collapsed (Klarna -85%, Affirm -90%).

records.name: MainStreaming (Insolvency)
records.failure_reason: Liquidation & Asset Sale
records.lesson: Milan video-streaming infrastructure startup MainStreaming filed liquidation in 2024 after over a decade trying to compete with hyperscale CDNs.

records.name: Supplyme
records.failure_reason: Failed to Find PMF in Italian SMBs
records.lesson: Turin B2B SaaS Supplyme failed to scale Italian SMB procurement and shut down in 2023 — representative of dozens of small Italian SaaS failures of the early-2020s wave.

records.name: Depop (Etsy Write-Down)
records.failure_reason: Etsy Acquisition Write-Down
records.lesson: Italian-founded fashion-marketplace Depop was acquired by Etsy for $1.6B in 2021, then written down by 50%+ within two years as Etsy struggled to integrate it.

records.name: YOOX Net-A-Porter (Richemont Write-Down)
records.failure_reason: Strategic Failure & €2.7B Impairment
records.lesson: Milan-founded luxury e-commerce pioneer YOOX-Net-A-Porter was written down by Richemont by €2.7B in 2023 then sold to Mytheresa at a near-zero price — the largest Italian e-commerce value destruction.

records.name: Milkman (Insolvency)
records.failure_reason: Last-Mile Unit Economics
records.lesson: Milan last-mile-delivery startup Milkman raised €30M then filed for restructuring in 2024 as Italian last-mile delivery unit economics collapsed.

records.name: Treedom (Layoffs & Restructure)
records.failure_reason: Corporate ESG Spending Pullback
records.lesson: Florence climate-tech Treedom, after raising €15M, conducted significant layoffs in 2024 as corporate ESG spending pulled back globally.

records.name: SmileDirectClub
records.failure_reason: Regulatory fights, dentist opposition, unit-economics collapse post-IPO
records.investors: Kleiner Perkins, Clayton Dubilier & Rice, public markets (NASDAQ: SDC)
records.lesson: Regulated categories don't reward 'move fast and break things'. SDC's IPO peak was $8.9B; investor dentists and 30+ state dental boards eventually broke the D2C aligner model.

records.name: Cue Health
records.failure_reason: Post-Covid demand collapse, FDA authorization issues, cash-out failure
records.investors: Decheng Capital, Madrone Capital, ACME Capital, public markets (NASDAQ: HLTH)
records.lesson: Pandemic-boom hardware companies rarely survive normalisation. Cue's at-home molecular test was clinically excellent but had no non-Covid demand curve.

records.name: Plastiq
records.failure_reason: SPAC deal collapse, failed to reach profitability in embedded finance
records.investors: Kleiner Perkins, Khosla Ventures, Top Tier Capital, Accomplice
records.lesson: SPAC merger cancellations often precede bankruptcy: they represent the last public-market signal that professional investors won't underwrite a business at claimed value.

records.name: Tally
records.failure_reason: Failed to raise follow-on round, high cost of consumer credit under rising rates
records.investors: Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Kleiner Perkins, Sway Ventures, Cowboy Ventures
records.lesson: a16z-scale funding doesn't inoculate against category math: consumer-credit refinancers can't out-earn the interest rates they refinance at when their own cost of capital rises.

records.name: Modsy
records.failure_reason: Post-pandemic e-commerce home spending crash + service unit economics never worked
records.investors: Norwest Venture Partners, Comcast Ventures, GV, TCV, BBG Ventures
records.lesson: Marketplace + service hybrids rarely reach margin at consumer prices. Modsy's $89 room design fee never covered the human-hour cost of a 3D-rendered layout.

records.name: Parse (Facebook)
records.industry: SaaS / Mobile Backend as a Service
records.failure_reason: Strategic abandonment by Facebook after 2013 acquisition; open-sourced and shut down
records.investors: Y Combinator, Andreessen Horowitz, Google Ventures — acquired by Facebook in 2013
records.lesson: Building on a proprietary backend is a bet on the acquirer's roadmap. When Facebook shifted focus, thousands of apps had to migrate in 12 months.

records.name: Rain AI
records.failure_reason: Failed $150M fundraise despite Sam Altman backing; forced sale
records.investors: Sam Altman (personal), Prosperity7 Ventures, Baidu Ventures, Grep VC
records.lesson: AI-hardware startups need billions to challenge NVIDIA. Rain's brain-inspired chip design was novel but couldn't out-run TSMC-scale capex on a $118M budget.

records.name: Synapse Financial
records.failure_reason: BaaS ledger collapse froze $265M of consumer deposits across Yotta, Juno, Copper and others
records.investors: Andreessen Horowitz, Trinity Ventures, Core Innovation Capital
records.lesson: BaaS middleware failures have systemic consequences: 100,000+ Americans lost access to $265M in deposits when Synapse's reconciliation collapsed with Evolve Bank.

records.name: Plenty Unlimited
records.failure_reason: Vertical farming unit economics never worked at scale; last-ditch pivot to strawberries too late
records.investors: SoftBank Vision Fund, Jeff Bezos (Bezos Expeditions), Walmart, DCM Ventures, Driscoll's
records.lesson: The third $1B vertical farming failure of the decade (after AeroFarms and Infarm). LED + labour + water costs kept category unit economics permanently negative at consumer prices.

records.name: Flip (TikTok Rival)
records.failure_reason: Failed to reach TikTok-scale engagement; social commerce economics never justified $1B valuation
records.investors: GV, Streamlined Ventures, Institutional Venture Partners (IVP)
records.lesson: Direct TikTok clones with paid GMV incentives can juice topline but not creator retention. Flip's $1B valuation assumed viral organic growth that never happened.

records.name: Fair.com (Car Subscription)
records.failure_reason: SoftBank-scale funding met catastrophic unit economics on used-car depreciation
records.lesson: Fair burned $2.1B on the belief that a weekly car-subscription would unlock rideshare drivers. When Uber renegotiated the partnership in 2020, the volume base disappeared overnight.

records.name: Bitfront (LINE)
records.failure_reason: Strategic exit by parent LINE Corp; crypto winter and FTX contagion
records.lesson: Corporate-parent crypto exchanges shut down first when the parent's core business faces pressure — Bitfront closed 5 months after FTX collapsed.

records.name: Corinthian Colleges
records.failure_reason: CFPB and DOE fraud investigations; predatory lending scheme against low-income students
records.lesson: Business models built on federal student-loan arbitrage collapse when regulators finally act. Corinthian's students received $480M+ in federal loan discharges — the largest borrower-defense relief in US history at the time.

records.name: LeSports (LeEco Sports)
records.failure_reason: Parent company LeEco's cash crisis; over-paid sports rights collapsed
records.investors: LeEco (parent), Yunfeng Capital (Jack Ma), Legend Capital
records.lesson: China's second-largest sports rights collapse of the 2010s. LeSports paid unsustainable prices for Premier League and NBA rights that its parent LeEco couldn't cover.

records.name: Digital River (SaaS Division)
records.failure_reason: Loss of anchor Microsoft contract; commoditisation of Merchant-of-Record services
records.lesson: Merchant-of-Record providers depend on 1-2 anchor clients for 30-60% of revenue. Losing Microsoft in 2023 removed Digital River's revenue base while Stripe/Paddle competed for what remained.

records.name: Byju's (Global Collapse)
records.failure_reason: Insolvency proceedings on BCCI petition; largest edtech collapse in history
records.investors: Naspers/Prosus, Tiger Global, General Atlantic, Sequoia, BlackRock, Silver Lake
records.lesson: Byju's collapse is the most-cited edtech unravelling in history: $6B+ raised, $22B peak valuation, insolvency triggered by a $19M cricket-board sponsorship default.

records.name: Dash
records.failure_reason: Mismanagement & Missing Funds
records.lesson: Ghanaian-founded, Nigeria-active payments startup Dash raised US$33M in seed (largest ever in Africa at the time) then was wound down by investors after $25M+ went unaccounted.

records.name: 54gene
records.failure_reason: Strategic Confusion & Founder Departure
records.investors: Adjuvant Capital, Cathay AfricInvest, Y Combinator
records.lesson: Africa's most-funded genomics startup, 54gene, shut down after founder departed amid governance disputes and capital exhaustion.

records.name: Lazerpay
records.failure_reason: Failed to Raise Seed & Crypto Winter
records.lesson: Nigerian crypto-payments startup Lazerpay shut down after a year, a representative case of African crypto startups hit by both crypto winter and Nigerian regulatory crackdowns.
