records.name: OkHi (Pivot/Wind-Down)
records.failure_reason: Slow B2B Sales Cycles
records.lesson: Kenyan-Nigerian addressing startup OkHi raised US$8M to digitize African addresses then largely wound down as banks built in-house solutions.

records.name: Vibra
records.failure_reason: Crypto Winter & Regulation
records.lesson: Nigerian crypto-exchange Vibra shut down in 2023, another casualty of the African crypto regulatory crackdown.

records.name: Thepeer
records.failure_reason: Slow Adoption & Failed Product-Market Fit
records.lesson: Lagos B2B fintech-API startup Thepeer shut down in April 2024 after failing to find sufficient adoption — a transparent founder post-mortem.

records.name: Doohickey AI
records.failure_reason: Product-market fit, rapid AI changes
records.lesson: Even accelerator pedigree and fresh VC capital can't save a startup that hasn't nailed product-market fit before the underlying technology landscape shifts beneath it.

records.name: Chemovator
records.failure_reason: Corporate restructuring and cost-cutting
records.lesson: Corporate venture-building units live and die by the parent company's financial health and strategic priorities—strong execution doesn't guarantee survival when the corporate parent needs to cut costs.

records.name: Trela
records.failure_reason: Failed to close funding round; capital-intensive logistics unsustainable
records.lesson: Just-in-time grocery in emerging markets still eats capital faster than it generates margin — Trela's efficient model wasn't enough once Brazilian LatAm funding tightened and rivals also retreated.

records.name: Entropy
records.failure_reason: Failed to reach venture-scale growth; returning capital to investors
records.lesson: Even top-tier crypto funding doesn't guarantee product-market fit — a16z-backed Entropy chose to wind down and return capital rather than pivot again, illustrating discipline over survival theater.

records.name: Parker
records.failure_reason: Bankruptcy, acquisition talks failed
records.lesson: Over-hiring and reactive decisions can lead to financial instability, even for well-funded startups with significant revenue.

records.name: Prime 7 Bar & Restaurant
records.failure_reason: Bankruptcy filing (Chapter 11)
records.lesson: Even beloved, high-traffic restaurants can collapse under debt and rising costs; hospitality businesses need disciplined capital structures to survive seasonal and economic swings.

records.name: Dunzo
records.failure_reason: Mounting debt, failed competition
records.lesson: Even significant funding and strategic investors cannot guarantee survival against intense competition and financial mismanagement in a high-burn industry.

records.name: BluSmart
records.failure_reason: Founder fraud (SEBI probe), diverted loan funds, cash crunch
records.lesson: Lack of corporate governance and financial impropriety can swiftly lead to the collapse of a promising startup, regardless of its market potential.

records.name: Hike
records.failure_reason: Pivot to real-money gaming banned by India
records.investors: Tiger Global, SoftBank, Tencent, Foxconn, Bharti SoftBank
records.lesson: Unicorn status doesn't insulate a startup from a single regulatory shock — Hike's post-messaging pivot into Rush Gaming was wiped out overnight when India banned real-money games in 2025.

records.name: Good Glamm Group
records.failure_reason: Cash crunch, failed refinancing, lenders forced brand-by-brand sale
records.investors: Prosus, Warburg Pincus, L'Occitane, Bessemer, Accel
records.lesson: A roll-up 'house of brands' only works if the parent can service debt and integrate acquisitions — when a single anchor deal fell through, Good Glamm's entire capital stack collapsed and lenders dismantled the unicorn brand by brand.

records.name: Otipy
records.failure_reason: Quick-commerce killed the model; failed to close new funding round
records.investors: WestBridge Capital, SIG, Omidyar Network, Cornerstone Venture Partners
records.lesson: 10-minute delivery reset consumer expectations across Indian grocery — Otipy's next-day farm-to-fork model became structurally uncompetitive against Blinkit and Zepto no matter how efficient its logistics were.

records.name: Subtl.AI
records.failure_reason: Lack of focus, poor product-market fit
records.lesson: A clear, narrow market focus and a credible path to your next funding round matter as much as the technology itself — especially in crowded, fast-moving categories like generative AI.

records.name: Monarch Tractor
records.failure_reason: Hardware unit economics, failed pivot to software, dealer lawsuits
records.investors: Astanor Ventures, CNH Industrial, Foothill Ventures, HH-CTBC
records.lesson: Full-stack hardware startups need a working commercial product before pivoting to software — Monarch's $100K autonomous tractors underdelivered, dealer lawsuits piled up, and the software pivot came too late to save the company.

records.name: Sonex Aircraft
records.failure_reason: Severe drop-off in sales, bank pressure
records.lesson: A long operating history and loyal niche customer base don't protect a manufacturer from a liquidity crisis — sustained unprofitability plus a credit pullback can force an immediate shutdown with little warning.

records.name: Epic Lightning Fast Service LLC
records.failure_reason: Challenging market conditions
records.lesson: In cyclical industries like trucking and logistics, sustained rate downturns can force even operationally sound companies to close — building in financial buffers for prolonged market downturns is essential.

records.name: Hycan Auto
records.failure_reason: Product misfires, unpaid severance, parent GAC pulled support
records.investors: GAC Group, NIO (early), Pearl River Investment Management
records.lesson: Even a joint venture between two well-known EV players can die when neither parent fully commits — Hycan was orphaned when NIO exited and GAC deprioritized it as its own Aion and Trumpchi brands took priority.

records.name: HiPhi
records.failure_reason: Cash crunch, failed to compete with BYD/Tesla in China EV price war
records.investors: Human Horizons, Ping An, state-linked investors
records.lesson: Chinese luxury EV upstarts couldn't survive the BYD-led price war — HiPhi burned through $1B+ chasing a premium positioning that collapsed the moment scaled incumbents cut prices.

records.name: Altigreen
records.failure_reason: Cash crunch, unpaid dues to vendors and employees, halted manufacturing
records.investors: Reliance New Energy, Sixth Sense Ventures, Xponentia Capital
records.lesson: Being early in Indian commercial EVs isn't a moat when incumbents (Mahindra, Bajaj, Piaggio) launch competitive electric 3-wheelers with dealer networks and financing — Altigreen ran out of runway before scale.

records.name: ANS Commerce
records.failure_reason: Acquirer Flipkart wound up operations
records.lesson: Being acquired by a large strategic buyer doesn't guarantee long-term survival — if the underlying unit economics don't improve post-acquisition, parent companies will shut down even previously well-funded businesses.

records.name: Astra
records.failure_reason: SPAC value destruction; take-private at a tiny fraction of peak valuation
records.investors: Founders (Chris Kemp, Adam London), ACME Capital, Marc Benioff
records.lesson: SPAC-fueled launch companies confused market cap for capability — Astra's rockets couldn't repeatedly reach orbit, and public shareholders wore the entire loss when founders bought it back for pennies.

records.name: Beepkart
records.failure_reason: Funding winter, unit economics, failed to raise follow-on
records.lesson: Used two-wheeler resale requires deep working capital and margin discipline — BeepKart couldn't outlast India's 2024-25 funding winter, and mass layoffs preceded a quiet asset-sale exit rather than a going-concern shutdown.

records.name: BharatAgri
records.failure_reason: Failed to close $6-8M round; funding winter for Indian agritech
records.lesson: Advisory-only agritech models struggle to monetize Indian farmers directly — BharatAgri couldn't reach profitability before capital dried up in an 80%-down agritech funding cycle.

records.name: Blip
records.failure_reason: Lack of capital for expansion
records.lesson: Applying a proven business model (like quick-commerce) to a new category doesn't guarantee success — fashion's inventory and operational complexity requires far more capital before viable unit economics.

records.name: CodeParrot
records.failure_reason: High cash burn, lack of follow-on funding
records.lesson: YC acceptance and a hot AI category aren't enough — startups still need disciplined burn management and a credible path to differentiated, defensible value before the funding window closes.

records.name: NeuroPixel.AI
records.failure_reason: Cash crunch
records.lesson: Building a genuinely innovative vertical AI product isn't enough protection — if your core capability can be replicated by general-purpose foundation models, you need a defensible moat beyond the technology itself.

records.name: Covrzy
records.failure_reason: Cash crunch
records.lesson: Startups with thin funding cushions are highly vulnerable to key personnel departures; when acquisition offers arrive during a cash crunch, rejecting them can foreclose the only viable exit.

records.name: Kiki
records.failure_reason: Unsustainable business economics
records.lesson: Persistent pivoting without achieving product-market fit, even with sufficient funding and years of runway, is a strong predictor of eventual failure — especially when core customers remain confused about the business model.

records.name: Ascend Elements
records.failure_reason: Chapter 11 amid EV demand slowdown and rollback of clean-energy incentives
records.investors: Decarbonization Partners (BlackRock/Temasek), SK ecoplant, Qatar Investment Authority, Fifth Wall
records.lesson: Cleantech scale-ups with government-loan-and-EV-demand assumptions baked in are one policy shift away from insolvency — Ascend's $900M+ raise couldn't outrun the 2025-26 EV slowdown and Trump-era incentive rollback.

records.name: The Next Web
records.failure_reason: Parent FT wound down events/media business amid AI-driven traffic decline
records.lesson: AI search is compressing tech-media traffic faster than legacy owners can restructure — the FT quietly killed one of Europe's most-loved conferences rather than fund another year of losses.

records.name: The Browser Co.
records.failure_reason: Arc browser abandoned; sold to Atlassian after failing to scale
records.investors: Thrive Capital, LinkedIn co-founders, Salesforce Ventures, Medha Ventures
records.lesson: Loved doesn't mean adopted. Arc had a cult following but never crossed into mainstream distribution, forcing The Browser Company to abandon it, pivot to an AI browser (Dia), and ultimately sell to Atlassian rather than reach standalone escape velocity.

records.name: CaaStle
records.failure_reason: Alleged $300M investor fraud by CEO, Chapter 7 bankruptcy
records.investors: Founders Fund, Bain Capital Ventures, Fidelity, Franklin Templeton
records.lesson: Fabricating financials to keep raising doesn't buy time — it converts a struggling business into a criminal case and wipes out every stakeholder. CaaStle went from unicorn to Chapter 7 liquidation once auditors uncovered years of forged bank statements.

records.name: PosiGen
records.failure_reason: Chapter 11 amid high interest rates, tariff shock, TPO/ITC policy uncertainty
records.investors: Brookfield Asset Management, Builders VC, Osaic, DBL Partners
records.lesson: Even mission-aligned installers can't outrun rate shock and policy whiplash — PosiGen's LMI-focused solar leases were structurally sound but its capital stack couldn't survive 2025's cost-of-capital repricing.

records.name: Synapse Financial Technologies
records.failure_reason: Chapter 11 collapse; ~$85M in end-user deposits went missing across partner banks
records.investors: Andreessen Horowitz, Trinity Ventures, Core Innovation Capital
records.lesson: BaaS middlemen created a systemic risk regulators never fully oversaw — Synapse's collapse froze 100,000+ Americans' savings and exposed the 'FDIC-insured' promise of fintech as marketing, not law.

records.name: Yotta Technologies
records.failure_reason: Deposits vanished after Synapse (BaaS provider) went bankrupt
records.investors: Base10 Partners, YC, Core Innovation Capital, FundersClub
records.lesson: A consumer fintech is only as trustworthy as its BaaS partner — Yotta customers followed the app's promises, not the actual bank of record, and were left with claims against a bankruptcy estate instead of insured deposits.

records.name: IO Biotech
records.failure_reason: Filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy
records.lesson: A single pivotal trial narrowly missing statistical significance can be as fatal to a biotech's near-term viability as an outright failure, especially when regulators require an entirely new registrational study.

records.name: Lipella Pharmaceuticals
records.failure_reason: Bankruptcy, inability to develop drug
records.lesson: Positive clinical trial data does not guarantee survival; without continued access to capital markets, even scientifically promising biotechs can be forced into bankruptcy.

records.name: Lipocine Inc.
records.failure_reason: Phase 3 trial failed primary endpoint
records.lesson: Repeated regulatory delays on a single lead drug can trigger a slow erosion of stock value and exchange compliance that persists for years, even if the company avoids outright shutdown.

records.name: Moleculin Biotech Inc.
records.failure_reason: Weak pipeline, funding contraction
records.lesson: Single-asset oncology biotechs remain acutely vulnerable to any negative trial readout, even when later data from more rigorous pivotal trials shows more encouraging results.

records.name: Nine Square Therapeutics
records.failure_reason: Liquidity crisis, funding standstill
records.investors: Apple Tree Partners, The Michael J. Fox Foundation
records.lesson: Even well-funded platform biotechs targeting scientifically validated but historically undruggable targets can run out of runway if they cannot translate discovery into a compelling near-term catalyst.

records.name: Nido Biosciences
records.failure_reason: Drug failed Phase II clinical trial
records.investors: 5AM Ventures, Abingworth, Bessemer Venture Partners, Eli Lilly, Osage University Partners, Bioluminescence Ventures
records.lesson: Even well-capitalized biotechs backed by reputable venture studios can be forced to shut down entirely when a single Phase 2 trial in a rare disease indication underperforms.

records.name: Builder.ai
records.failure_reason: Builder.ai, a Microsoft-backed 'AI-powered' app development platform once valued at $1.5 billion, collapsed into insolvency after revelations that its 'AI' was largely human engineers and that revenue
records.lesson: Marketing an unproven or partially fake AI capability to inflate valuation is unsustainable — eventually revenue, technology, and reality must align, or collapse follows.

records.name: Northvolt
records.failure_reason: Northvolt, Europe's flagship EV battery champion once valued at over $10 billion, filed for bankruptcy in Sweden in March 2025 after burning through more than $15 billion in funding without reaching s
records.lesson: Raising enormous capital cannot substitute for proven manufacturing execution — hardware startups must de-risk production processes before scaling to gigafactory volumes.

records.name: 23andMe
records.failure_reason: Once valued at $6 billion, DNA testing pioneer 23andMe filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in March 2025 after a massive 2023 data breach, collapsing demand for one-time genetic tests, and failure to buil
records.lesson: Owning valuable data is not the same as owning a sustainable business model — and a single catastrophic breach of customer trust can be fatal for a company built on sensitive personal information.

records.name: Canoo
records.failure_reason: Electric vehicle startup Canoo filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy and ceased all operations in January 2025, liquidating its assets after years of production delays, executive turnover, and chronic cash s
records.lesson: SPAC hype and government or corporate pilot deals cannot substitute for proven, scalable manufacturing — EV startups need capital discipline and production execution.

records.name: Forward Health
records.failure_reason: Forward Health, a venture-backed primary care startup that raised over $650 million to build AI-powered 'CarePod' health kiosks, abruptly shut down all clinics and its app in late 2024, with the fallo
records.lesson: In healthcare, sudden business pivots and shutdowns carry a duty of care to patients — Forward's shift to CarePods and abrupt closure show that scaling ambition must be balanced against continuity of care.

records.name: Yupp
records.failure_reason: Growth stalled after novelty wore off; consumer LLM-comparison thesis couldn't sustain retention
records.investors: a16z crypto (Chris Dixon), Jerry Yang, Balaji Srinivasan, angels
records.lesson: A famous cap table and a hot thesis can't rescue a consumer product with no repeat-use loop. If DAU/WAU flattens 3 months post-launch, no amount of VC can fix it.

records.name: Zeepay
records.failure_reason: Ghana central bank revoked e-money issuer licence over prolonged solvency and governance failures
records.investors: Injaro Investments, Verdant Capital, Oikocredit, Goodwell Investments
records.lesson: In regulated fintech, your licence is your business. Missed capital ratios and governance lapses can end an entire company in a single regulator letter.

records.name: Gigbanc
records.failure_reason: Could not raise a follow-on round in a chilled Nigerian fintech funding market
records.lesson: Sub-$5M raised in a hard market means an 18-month runway if you are lucky. Line up the acquirer before you announce the wind-down.

records.name: AstrumU
records.failure_reason: Ran out of capital before enterprise sales cycles closed at scale
records.investors: Ignition Partners, Kickstart Fund, University Ventures
records.lesson: Selling to universities and enterprise HR at the same time is two 18-month sales cycles overlaid. Pick one buyer or you burn through both budgets.

records.name: Zeen (formerly Landing)
records.failure_reason: Never reached the scale required for a venture-backed consumer social business
records.lesson: If your app doesn't cross a million MAU after two pivots, no amount of aesthetic polish will unlock venture-scale outcomes. Return the money or sell the domain.

records.name: Smashing
records.failure_reason: Curation apps cannot compete with algorithmic feeds and AI summaries for consumer attention
records.lesson: 'A better feed' is not a business. Readers don't pay, ads need scale, and AI now writes the summary you built a company around.

records.name: Haomo.AI
records.failure_reason: Parent Great Wall Motor cut funding after failing to match Tesla FSD and BYD-backed rivals
records.investors: Great Wall Motor, Meituan Longzhu, Qualcomm Ventures, Gaocheng Capital
records.lesson: Corporate-backed AV spinouts live and die by the parent's roadmap. When GWM redirected to a partnership with a larger AV supplier, Haomo's mandate evaporated overnight.

records.name: Ample
records.failure_reason: Capital-intensive swap-station rollout outran a fleet-only revenue model
records.investors: Shell Ventures, Moore Strategic Ventures, PTT, Repsol, Blackstone-adjacent funds
records.lesson: Hardware + real estate + energy is three businesses in a trench coat. If you don't have OEM co-investment or utility rate-basing, the CapEx will bury you.

records.name: JiviAI
records.failure_reason: Ran out of runway before proving clinical adoption of a medical LLM
records.lesson: Selling AI into regulated healthcare requires 24+ months and hospital champions. If you can't clear that milestone with 18 months of runway, don't start.

records.name: Miga Health
records.failure_reason: Virtual specialty care model couldn't clear payer reimbursement thresholds
records.lesson: Virtual specialty clinics live or die on payer contracts. If your CPT-code strategy isn't proven in year one, your Series A math is fiction.

records.name: Joon Care
records.failure_reason: Consolidation into larger virtual mental-health platform via acqui-hire
records.lesson: If the category consolidates before you find defensible unit economics, taking the acqui-hire is the responsible ending, not the failure.

records.name: Kevala
records.failure_reason: Sub-scale point solution absorbed by broader senior-care platform
records.lesson: Vertical workforce SaaS with <$5M ARR gets acquired, not IPO'd. Design your cap table for a $30-80M exit from day one.

records.name: Ribbon Health
records.failure_reason: API-only data infrastructure absorbed into vertical analytics leader
records.investors: a16z, General Catalyst, Rock Health, Homebrew
records.lesson: Being 'the data layer' is a great narrative and a hard business. If a bigger analytics buyer needs your data more than you need to be a company, sell.

records.name: Onco
records.failure_reason: Sub-scale patient acquisition led to a quiet strategic acquisition by Apollo Hospitals
records.lesson: In Indian health-tech, the exit is the largest hospital chain, not the IPO. Build for strategic value from year two.

records.name: Kismet Health
records.failure_reason: Acquired by Kooth for its telehealth platform, ending standalone operations
records.lesson: A specialized telehealth toolset can be worth more inside a larger buyer than as a standalone SaaS. Recognize the tuck-in ceiling early.

records.name: Satori Finance
records.failure_reason: Unable to capture liquidity share against Hyperliquid and dYdX in perps DEX category
records.lesson: In DeFi, liquidity is a winner-take-most flywheel. If you're not top-3 by TVL 12 months post-launch, you're kindling.

records.name: Goldfinch Finance
records.failure_reason: Real-world credit defaults exceeded protocol loss-absorption capacity
records.investors: a16z crypto, Coinbase Ventures, Bill Ackman, Kindred Ventures
records.lesson: On-chain credit protocols inherit off-chain default risk without off-chain collections. Assume 5-10x higher realized losses than TradFi comps.

records.name: AscendEX
records.failure_reason: Liquidity crisis compounded by unexplained founder silence
records.investors: Polychain Capital, Alameda Research, Hack VC
records.lesson: Custody businesses run on trust. Any founder communication gap during a liquidity event triggers a bank-run, whether or not the balance sheet supports it.

records.name: Sophon
records.failure_reason: zkSync-based L2 could not attract users or developers; pivoted to Base app studio
records.investors: Node-sale participants, Aave GHO Foundation, Paper Ventures
records.lesson: 'Build a chain' is a distribution problem, not a technology problem. If you raise via node sale before proving app-layer traction, you owe explanations to token holders when you pivot away.

records.name: PeopleCues
records.failure_reason: Employee-experience SaaS could not survive the 2025-2026 HR tech budget freeze
records.investors: Binny Bansal (Flipkart co-founder), Peak XV, angels
records.lesson: HR tech is the first budget line cut in a downturn. Ship must-have workflow, not surveys, if you want to survive a spend freeze.

records.name: Mantle
records.failure_reason: AI-powered Shopify app tooling could not build a defensible business layer
records.lesson: Building 'infrastructure for a platform's developers' is a tiny TAM. Shopify's own tooling improvements erase your wedge overnight.

records.name: Talrop
records.failure_reason: AI-driven curriculum obsolescence and financial mismanagement
records.lesson: EdTech curricula that teach a skill AI now does are graveyards. If your syllabus needs a rewrite every 6 months to stay relevant, your unit economics won't survive.

records.name: Wordsworth AI
records.failure_reason: Six-figure revenue was not enough to justify continued operation as market shifted
records.lesson: Six-figure ARR with enterprise customers is a lifestyle business, not a venture case. Recognize the ceiling and either bootstrap or wind down honestly.

records.name: Pocket (Mozilla)
records.failure_reason: Parent Mozilla sunset the acquired product amid strategic refocus
records.investors: Mozilla (2017 acquirer), previously Foundation Capital, Google Ventures
records.lesson: Being acquired is not the finish line. If the parent's strategy changes, your product is a line-item to be cut.

records.name: Rewind AI
records.failure_reason: Rebrand to Limitless AI pendant hardware led to Meta acquisition and sunset of original Mac app
records.investors: a16z, First Round Capital, NEA, Sam Altman
records.lesson: A hardware pivot away from a beloved consumer software product is the highest-risk restart in tech. Get the acquisition offer before you tell your users.

records.name: iRobot
records.failure_reason: Failed Amazon acquisition + Chinese Roomba clones destroyed pricing power
records.investors: Public shareholders; formerly funded by Fenway Partners; ended in Picea (Chinese contract manufacturer) ownership
records.lesson: A pending acquisition is not an insurance policy. Regulatory blocks kill your Plan B. If your product is a commoditized SKU, an EU antitrust ruling can end your independence.

records.name: Picnic
records.failure_reason: Food-service labor economics didn't justify $100k+ pizza-assembly robots
records.lesson: Automation ROI must beat minimum-wage plus benefits, in the counterfactual, not in the pitch deck. Pizza labor is $15/hr — that's a $30k/year threshold no six-figure robot beats.

records.name: Cartwheel Robotics
records.failure_reason: Ran out of capital before completing seed round for capital-intensive humanoid hardware
records.lesson: Humanoid robotics is a $100M seed category disguised as a $3M seed category. Don't start unless you have signed commitments from Series A leads before shipping.

records.name: Locus Robotics
records.failure_reason: Robots-as-a-Service unit economics never turned positive at scale
records.investors: Tiger Global, Prologis, Zebra Ventures, G2 Venture Partners
records.lesson: RaaS gross margins < hardware gross margins < software gross margins. If your Series F pitched software multiples on RaaS revenue, the Series G markdown is brutal.

records.name: Lidya
records.failure_reason: Loan-book losses combined with FX collapse eroded the equity base
records.investors: Alitheia Capital, Bamboo Capital, Newid Capital, Omidyar Network
records.lesson: Digital lending in an FX-volatile market requires local-currency capital. Dollar-denominated equity funding a naira loan book is a losing trade every devaluation cycle.

records.name: Okra
records.failure_reason: Open-banking API infrastructure couldn't reach revenue scale in Nigerian market challenges
records.investors: Susa Ventures, TLcom Capital, Base10 Partners, Accenture Ventures
records.lesson: If your business is 'the Plaid of X,' you need a Plaid-sized banking ecosystem with regulator-mandated open banking. Nigeria didn't have that in 2019-2025.

records.name: Cushion
records.failure_reason: Consumer fintech unit economics couldn't scale beyond niche users
records.investors: Flourish Ventures, Left Lane Capital, angel investors
records.lesson: 'AI negotiates your bank fees' works as a demo. It doesn't work as a business because banks won't pay the arbitrage forever, and consumers won't pay for a service that returns their own money.

records.name: The Sandbox
records.failure_reason: Metaverse user base collapsed; Animoca Brands absorbed operations after 50%+ layoffs
records.investors: Animoca Brands (parent), SoftBank, LG Tech Ventures
records.lesson: If your product depends on 'the metaverse,' your business depends on a category that peaked in Q4 2021 and hasn't returned. Cut before the parent has to.

records.name: Ember Sword
records.failure_reason: Crypto game economics collapsed; virtual land holders lost value
records.lesson: Selling virtual land before a game is playable is fundraising, not product development. When the game doesn't ship, the SEC and the pitchforks come.

records.name: Battlebound
records.failure_reason: Blockchain-gaming category couldn't retain players between hype cycles
records.investors: Delphi Digital, Merit Circle, Play Ventures
records.lesson: If your monetization requires token liquidity that requires new players that requires token liquidity, you have built a fragile flywheel that stops in month 6.

records.name: Tatsumeeko: Lumina Fates
records.failure_reason: Play-to-earn MMORPG couldn't build a Web2-quality game on a Web3-sized team
records.investors: Delphi Digital, Signum Capital, Animoca Brands, Ascensive Assets
records.lesson: An MMORPG is a $50M+ dev budget. A $7.5M seed for an MMORPG means you'll ship the tokenomics and never ship the game.

records.name: Pandion
records.failure_reason: Middle-mile parcel network couldn't win volume from Amazon Logistics or FedEx SmartPost
records.investors: Playground Global, Kleiner Perkins, Prologis, SoftBank
records.lesson: Building a national parcel network without a captive shipper is the hardest capital allocation problem in tech. Convoy tried and failed. Pandion tried and failed. Don't try.

records.name: Pedal & Post
records.failure_reason: Loss of anchor Voi contract eliminated majority of revenue overnight
records.lesson: Customer concentration >50% is a single-point-of-failure. When your anchor gives notice, you have 30-60 days to become a different company.

records.name: Ami Colé
records.failure_reason: D2C beauty economics collapsed under retail-competition and marketing cost inflation
records.investors: Imaginary Ventures, Debut Capital, angel investors
records.lesson: Being a beloved indie brand isn't a business. If you can't defend >50% gross margin with paid CAC below $60, close before you owe suppliers.

records.name: 10Club
records.failure_reason: Thrasio playbook collapsed globally; India aggregators inherited the debt without the exit path
records.investors: Fireside Ventures, DisruptAD, Sequoia India, MSCT Investments
records.lesson: 'Buying up Amazon sellers' was a 2021 zero-rate-era thesis. Every aggregator in every market underestimated integration costs and overestimated multiples.

records.name: Areteia Therapeutics
records.failure_reason: Phase 3 asthma studies terminated for insufficient efficacy
records.investors: Population Health Partners, Bain Capital Life Sciences, Access Industries
records.lesson: A $425M startup bet on a single molecule is a coin-flip. Diversify the shots on goal or pre-commit to wind-down triggers investors will actually honor.

records.name: iTeos Therapeutics
records.failure_reason: GSK terminated TIGIT partnership after negative Phase 2 lung cancer data
records.investors: Public shareholders (Nasdaq: ITOS); MPM Capital, Novo Holdings previously
records.lesson: Big-pharma partnerships aren't insurance. GSK, Merck and Roche have all walked away from TIGIT programs. If your thesis is 'partner data will validate us,' the partner's decision terminates you.

records.name: Mythic Therapeutics
records.failure_reason: Bridge round failed; single ADC clinical trial terminated for funding reasons
records.investors: Venrock, Viking Global, Rock Springs, Cowen Healthcare Investments
records.lesson: A single-asset biotech's Series C is the last cheque. If Phase 1/2 data isn't remarkable, don't expect a Series D at any price.

records.name: Inspirna
records.failure_reason: Failed to raise Phase 3 funding; folded before pivotal trial
records.investors: Deerfield Management, Cormorant Asset Management, Woodline Partners
records.lesson: If you can't fund the Phase 3 you designed, the design was wrong. Downsize the trial or partner years earlier.

records.name: Sensei Biotherapeutics
records.failure_reason: Dropped sole clinical program to conserve remaining cash before shell status
records.investors: Public shareholders (Nasdaq: SNSE); Cormorant, RA Capital previously
records.lesson: If you're a $30M-market-cap public biotech that just failed a readout, don't burn what's left. Return cash, become a shell, or reverse-merge.

records.name: theGist
records.failure_reason: Product commoditized by native features in Slack, Google Workspace and ChatGPT
records.lesson: If your product summarizes Slack or Gmail, Slack and Gmail will summarize themselves within 12 months. Choose a defensible wedge or die on the platform update.

records.name: Dot (New Computer)
records.failure_reason: Consumer AI companion market couldn't sustain subscription retention
records.lesson: Companion apps have Tinder-like uninstall rates. If your product depends on emotional connection with a chatbot, expect 90% churn at day 30.

records.name: Chimoney
records.failure_reason: Under-capitalized global payments infrastructure with weak distribution
records.lesson: Global payments infrastructure is a $50M-minimum business. A $1M seed can't win licences, banking partners or distribution simultaneously.

records.name: Medial
records.failure_reason: Couldn't monetize a 500k-user social network before capital ran out
records.investors: Shark Tank India investors, Peak XV alumni angels
records.lesson: 500k users is not a business. Consumer social with no ads, no subscription and no marketplace ends when the seed runs out — every time.

records.name: Humane
records.failure_reason: Product-market fit collapse; laser-projector wearable rejected by reviewers
records.investors: Kindred Ventures, Marc Benioff, Sam Altman, Microsoft, LG, SoftBank, Tiger Global
records.lesson: A hardware moonshot needs a job that a phone cannot already do better. The AI Pin lost every side-by-side comparison against a smartphone.

records.name: Fisker Inc.
records.failure_reason: Manufacturing chaos, software failures, and cash burn on the Ocean SUV
records.lesson: Contract-manufacturing an EV without owning software integration is a recipe for recall hell. Second-time founders are not automatic proof of execution.

records.name: Cruise (Robotaxi)
records.failure_reason: Regulatory revocation, safety incident cover-up, and $2B+ annual burn shut by GM
records.investors: General Motors, SoftBank Vision Fund, Honda, Microsoft, T. Rowe Price
records.lesson: Autonomy is a decade-plus, capital-black-hole problem. When a single incident and a cover-up destroy regulator trust, no amount of parent-company cash can restart the flywheel.

records.name: Lilium
records.failure_reason: Insolvency after German government refused €100M loan guarantee; ducted-fan design never certified
records.investors: Tencent, Baillie Gifford, LGT, Atomico, Frank Thelen, Public markets (SPAC)
records.lesson: Betting the company on a technically ambitious design and a single government backstop is not a strategy. Certification, not renderings, is the eVTOL moat.

records.name: Volocopter
records.failure_reason: Insolvency after failing to certify VoloCity before Paris 2024 and running out of runway
records.investors: Geely, Daimler, Intel Capital, BlackRock, DB Schenker
records.lesson: "Launch at the Olympics" is a marketing plan, not a certification plan. Missing a hyped date destroyed Volocopter's ability to raise the next round.

records.name: Bench Accounting
records.failure_reason: Cash crunch and negative unit economics on bundled human bookkeeping; assets acquired by Employer.com
records.investors: Bain Capital Ventures, Shopify, Altos Ventures, iNovia, Sage
records.lesson: Human-labor SaaS looks like SaaS on the surface until you look at gross margin. Bench's margins never supported its growth spend.

records.name: 2U Inc.
records.failure_reason: Chapter 11 after Online Program Manager revenue-share model collapsed under university pushback and Dept. of Ed rules
records.investors: Bessemer, Redpoint, Highland Capital, Public markets
records.lesson: Regulatory arbitrage is not a business model. When the US Department of Education signals it will kill your revenue share, your equity has already been destroyed.

records.name: Invitae
records.failure_reason: Chapter 11 after unsustainable land-grab pricing on genetic tests and $1.5B ArcherDX acquisition debt
records.investors: ARCH Venture Partners, Genesys Capital, SoftBank, Public markets
records.lesson: Buying market share by pricing tests below cost only works if you find profitable adjacencies before the debt bill comes due. Invitae never did.

records.name: Cano Health
records.failure_reason: Chapter 11 after acquisition-led expansion left it with $1B+ debt and negative cash flow
records.investors: InTandem Capital, Barry Sternlicht, Dan Loeb Third Point, Public markets (SPAC)
records.lesson: Roll-up healthcare growth funded by debt is not "value-based care" — it is leverage waiting for a rate cycle to end it.

records.name: Nikola Corporation
records.failure_reason: Chapter 11 after years of fraud fallout, truck fires, and unsustainable cash burn on hydrogen infrastructure
records.investors: Public markets (SPAC), CNH Industrial, Bosch, Iveco
records.lesson: Fraud at inception is a debt to reputation that keeps compounding. Even after Milton's conviction Nikola never recovered institutional trust.

records.name: Bowery Farming
records.failure_reason: Chapter 7 liquidation after vertical-farm unit economics never worked at scale
records.investors: GV, GGV, Fidelity, Temasek, General Catalyst
records.lesson: Growing lettuce indoors at grocery-shelf prices is a physics problem, not a software problem. Every VC-backed vertical farm has hit the same wall.

records.name: Plenty
records.failure_reason: Chapter 11 after strawberry pivot with Driscoll's failed to close unit-economics gap
records.investors: SoftBank Vision Fund, Jeff Bezos, Walmart, Driscoll's
records.lesson: Pivoting from lettuce to strawberries did not fix vertical-farming physics; it only bought Plenty one more round of runway.

records.name: Ghost Autonomy
records.failure_reason: Shutdown after failing to secure automaker deals and pivoting away from a viable ADAS wedge
records.investors: Founders Fund, Khosla Ventures, Coatue, Sutter Hill, OpenAI Startup Fund
records.lesson: OEMs do not buy revolutionary autonomy from tiny startups. Ghost died the moment it stopped selling to automakers on their terms.

records.name: Vroom
records.failure_reason: Wound down used-vehicle business after Carvana priced it out and unit economics collapsed
records.investors: T. Rowe Price, General Catalyst, Public markets
records.lesson: Being the #2 online used-car dealer during a rate cycle is the same as being dead. Vroom just took longer to realize it than the market.

records.name: Getir
records.failure_reason: Retreated from US, UK, Germany, Netherlands, Portugal, Spain, Italy in 2024 after 10-minute grocery model collapsed
records.lesson: Ten-minute grocery delivery is a marketing product that never generated ten-minute-grocery economics. The category compressed to zero in the West.

records.name: Bird Global
records.failure_reason: Chapter 11 after scooter unit economics, city permit costs and de-SPAC public listing destroyed the business
records.investors: Sequoia, Accel, Index, CDPQ, Tusk Ventures, Public markets (SPAC)
records.lesson: Being first in scooters was never a moat. Bird burned through nearly $900M proving that shared-scooter unit economics do not work at VC-required growth rates.

records.name: BeReal
records.failure_reason: Engagement collapse, no monetization, sold at fire-sale price
records.investors: Andreessen Horowitz, Accel, DST Global, New Wave
records.lesson: Viral hype is not a moat. A single-feature social app without monetization or daily engagement durability becomes worthless within 18 months.

records.name: Getir
records.failure_reason: Burnt cash on unit economics that never worked outside Turkey, ZIRP collapse
records.investors: Mubadala, Sequoia, Tiger Global, Silver Lake, Alkeon
records.lesson: Hyper-local 10-minute delivery is a structurally unprofitable category outside dense, low-wage markets. Geographic expansion multiplied losses instead of revenue.

records.name: Maple
records.failure_reason: Negative unit economics on $12 meals with full vertical integration
records.investors: Greenoaks Capital, Thrive Capital, David Chang, Bono
records.lesson: Owning the kitchen, the food, the riders and the customer all at once gives you control but also concentrates every loss. Vertical integration is not a strategy in low-margin categories.

records.name: Jibo
records.failure_reason: Three-year shipping delay, $899 price point, undercut by Alexa and Google Home
records.investors: RRE Ventures, CRV, Acer, Fenox Venture Capital
records.lesson: Hardware timelines are unforgiving. If you take three years to ship, the market you launched into will not exist when you arrive.

records.name: Vine
records.failure_reason: Twitter neglect, failed to monetize creators, lost talent to Instagram and YouTube
records.lesson: Owning the creators is more important than owning the format. Vine invented short-form video and lost it because it never paid them.

records.name: Yik Yak
records.failure_reason: Toxic content drove users away, then a pivot to identity killed what was left
records.investors: Sequoia Capital, DCM, Azure Capital, Renren
records.lesson: Anonymity drives both growth and abuse. If your community moderation can't scale faster than your user base, the platform poisons itself.

records.name: Compass
records.failure_reason: Brokerage with software paint never earned tech multiples; 90%+ value destruction post-IPO
records.investors: SoftBank Vision Fund, Fidelity, Wellington, Goldman Sachs
records.lesson: Calling yourself a tech company doesn't change your unit economics. Compass paid traditional brokerage commissions while spending tech-company money on software and recruiting.

records.name: The Messenger
records.failure_reason: Burned $50M in 8 months on a nonviable ad-supported general-news model
records.investors: Jimmy Finkelstein and undisclosed private investors
records.lesson: You cannot launch a large general-interest news publisher on advertising in 2023. The category economics are broken and no amount of senior hires can fix that.

records.name: Gorillas
records.failure_reason: Unprofitable dark-store model in Western Europe; absorbed by larger loss-maker
records.investors: DST Global, Tencent, Coatue, Atlantic Food Labs, Delivery Hero
records.lesson: Being the fastest in a category with broken unit economics just gets you to bankruptcy first.

records.name: Sprig
records.failure_reason: Vertically integrated meal delivery at $12 price points lost money on every order
records.investors: Greylock Partners, Accel Partners, Social+Capital, Battery Ventures
records.lesson: If your kitchen, your menu, your couriers and your app are all in-house, every single failure point is yours. In food delivery, that math doesn't work.

records.name: Bright Health
records.failure_reason: Catastrophic underwriting losses; forced to sell core insurance business to survive
records.investors: Bessemer Venture Partners, NEA, Greenspring, Tiger Global, Blackstone
records.lesson: Disrupting insurance with a tech UX doesn't help if your actuarial models are wrong. Bright underpriced risk by hundreds of millions every year.

records.name: Opendoor
records.failure_reason: Algorithm overpaid for homes in a falling market; lost ~$2B in 2022 alone
records.investors: SoftBank, GV, Khosla Ventures, NEA, Access Industries
records.lesson: When your business is buying assets and reselling them, mispricing risk by even 2% is catastrophic at scale. Opendoor's algorithm was wrong in exactly the wrong direction.

records.name: 23andMe
records.failure_reason: One-time DNA test had no recurring revenue; drug-discovery pivot failed; 2023 data breach destroyed trust
records.investors: Google Ventures, Sequoia, NEA, Johnson & Johnson, Richard Branson
records.lesson: A consumer product without recurring revenue is not a business. 23andMe sold a one-time spit kit to 14M people and never figured out what to do next.

records.name: Essential Products
records.failure_reason: Late launch, weak reviews, founder scandal, Apple/Samsung/Chinese OEM lock on the premium segment
records.investors: Andy Rubin, Tencent, Foxconn, Redpoint Ventures, Amazon Alexa Fund
records.lesson: The premium Android segment is closed. A new entrant needs more than a famous founder and good industrial design — it needs distribution, ecosystem and a roadmap the competition can't beat.

records.name: Flink
records.failure_reason: Burned through capital on the same broken 10-minute delivery model as Gorillas and Getir
records.investors: Mubadala, Prosus, REWE Group, Bond, DoorDash, Tiger Global
records.lesson: Being the 'last one standing' in a category that doesn't work isn't survival, it's just a slower exit.

records.name: Zulily
records.failure_reason: Flash-sales model lost to Amazon Prime; two waves of failure ending in liquidation
records.lesson: If your differentiator is 'cheaper than retail' in a world where Amazon is already cheaper than retail with two-day delivery, you don't have a business.

records.name: Honestbee
records.failure_reason: Unsustainable Unit Economics
records.lesson: Singapore's grocery-and-laundry on-demand pioneer expanded across SEA on $75M then ran out of cash with internal allegations of governance failures.

records.name: iPrice Group (Wind-Down)
records.failure_reason: Margin Compression & SEO Risk
records.investors: Line Ventures, Asia Venture Group, Gobi Partners
records.lesson: SEA price-comparison aggregator iPrice raised US$25M then largely wound down as marketplaces (Lazada, Shopee) cut affiliate payouts.

records.name: Vouch (Wind-Down)
records.failure_reason: Post-COVID Demand & Margin
records.lesson: Singapore hotel-SaaS Vouch raised US$11M then wound down as Asian hotel-tech budgets failed to recover post-COVID.

records.name: Carousell (Down Round & Layoffs)
records.failure_reason: Path to Profitability Pressure
records.lesson: Singapore unicorn Carousell laid off 10% of staff and accepted flat/down rounds as classifieds margins remained elusive.

records.name: Mfine Singapore (Wind-Down)
records.failure_reason: Post-COVID Demand Collapse
records.investors: SBI Investment, Beenext, Stellaris Venture Partners
records.lesson: Singapore-headquartered telehealth Mfine raised US$60M during COVID then heavily downsized as Asian telehealth demand normalized.

records.name: Vroom
records.failure_reason: Unit economics never worked online
records.investors: T. Rowe Price, General Catalyst, L Catterton, AutoNation
records.lesson: Selling used cars fully online sounds like a Carvana copy — but without the reconditioning throughput, it's just an unprofitable middleman.

records.name: Casper Sleep
records.failure_reason: CAC caught up with LTV in a commodity category
records.investors: IVP, NEA, Norwest, Lerer Hippeau, Target
records.lesson: A DTC 'lifestyle brand' becomes a mattress retailer the moment Facebook CPMs rise and 200 copycats appear.

records.name: Wag!
records.failure_reason: Two-sided marketplace beaten by Rover
records.investors: SoftBank Vision Fund, General Catalyst, Sherpa Capital
records.lesson: SoftBank capital can subsidize demand, but not fix a marketplace losing to a better-loved incumbent.

records.name: Blue Apron
records.failure_reason: Rising CAC and churn in a commodity category
records.lesson: A subscription business only works when reactivation is cheaper than acquisition — meal kits proved neither.

records.name: Groupon
records.failure_reason: Daily-deals model was structurally deflationary
records.investors: Accel, NEA, Kleiner Perkins, DST Global, Andreessen Horowitz
records.lesson: Selling merchants deep discounts trains customers to expect them and burns brand equity twice.

records.name: Zume
records.failure_reason: Robot pizza that never worked
records.lesson: SoftBank writing a $375M check does not mean the product exists — hardware, mobility and food safety all must actually work.

records.name: Anki
records.failure_reason: Consumer robotics burn out cash before scale
records.investors: Andreessen Horowitz, Index Ventures, Two Sigma
records.lesson: Beloved products die when a follow-on round doesn't close — consumer hardware needs 3+ years of runway per SKU.

records.name: Essential Products
records.failure_reason: Late launch into a saturated smartphone market
records.investors: Redpoint, Access Technology Ventures, Tencent, Foxconn, Amazon
records.lesson: 'Android founder makes new Android phone' isn't a value proposition to consumers — Samsung and Apple already own the shelf.

records.name: Coolest Cooler
records.failure_reason: Crowdfunding record couldn't overcome manufacturing math
records.lesson: A wildly successful Kickstarter can lock you into a per-unit price that guarantees losing money on every backer reward.

records.name: Juul Labs
records.failure_reason: Regulatory and litigation collapse of youth-vaping business
records.investors: Altria (35% stake at $12.8B), Fidelity, Tiger Global
records.lesson: If your growth relies on regulatory ambiguity and teen usage, the reckoning is only a matter of time — and it destroys everything.

records.name: Hampton Creek / JUST
records.failure_reason: Governance scandal and mass board resignation
records.investors: Khosla Ventures, Horizons Ventures, Founders Fund
records.lesson: When the board resigns en masse, the story is not the product — it's the founder.

records.name: Powa Technologies
records.failure_reason: Growth theater masking near-zero revenue
records.investors: Wellington Management, Otigo, ChinaNet Online Holdings
records.lesson: A $2.7B valuation on nine-figure funding is worthless if the underlying revenue was closer to $4M than $40M.

records.name: Made.com
records.failure_reason: Long lead times and inflation broke the model
records.lesson: A working-capital-intensive furniture business collapses instantly when shipping costs 5x and consumer demand halves.

records.name: Clinkle
records.failure_reason: Hype and founder drama with no shipping product
records.investors: Andreessen Horowitz, Peter Thiel, Marc Benioff, Richard Branson
records.lesson: A record seed round is a liability if you can't ship — every month past launch date compounds distrust.

records.name: Shyp
records.failure_reason: $5 flat rate priced below true cost
records.lesson: Charging a flat $5 to pick up, pack and ship anything guarantees losing money — you just don't know how much until you're big enough to matter.

records.name: Aereo
records.failure_reason: Supreme Court ruling killed the business overnight
records.investors: IAC (Barry Diller), Highland Capital, FirstMark Capital
records.lesson: If your entire business depends on a legal loophole, one Supreme Court decision is a company-ending event.

records.name: Jibo
records.failure_reason: Late shipment into a $199 Amazon Echo world
records.investors: RRE Ventures, CRV, Fenox, Osage University
records.lesson: If your $899 product ships three years late into a category defined by a $199 competitor, the reviews don't save you.

records.name: The Messenger
records.failure_reason: Ad-supported news at scale is not a business in 2024
records.investors: Jimmy Finkelstein and other private backers
records.lesson: Launching a general-interest news brand in a Google/Facebook duopoly and betting on programmatic ads is a nine-figure bet on a dying model.

records.name: Vine
records.failure_reason: Parent company neglect while TikTok caught up
records.lesson: Being acquired by a distracted parent can be worse than shutting down — you die slowly with a bigger audience watching.

records.name: Cazoo
records.failure_reason: SPAC-fueled expansion into a car market that didn't work online
records.investors: General Catalyst, D1 Capital, DST, Fidelity, Draper Esprit
records.lesson: The UK's biggest DTC unicorn couldn't overcome the reality that Britons still want to sit in a car before buying it.

records.name: Babylon Health
records.failure_reason: US value-based care expansion buried the AI-triage story
records.investors: Kinnevik, Vostok New Ventures, PIF, ERGO Group
records.lesson: Buying a US value-based-care book of business is a very expensive way to prove your AI triage isn't the business.

records.name: Britishvolt
records.failure_reason: Gigafactory ambition without customers or expertise
records.lesson: Announcing a £3.8B gigafactory before signing OEM offtake is theater — and theater doesn't fund payroll.

records.name: OVO Mobile
records.failure_reason: MVNO margins can't survive UK price wars
records.lesson: Selling mobile plans as a UK MVNO means competing with EE, O2 and Sky at their marginal cost of a SIM — an unwinnable game.

records.name: Deliveroo Australia
records.failure_reason: Third-place player exit in three-cornered market
records.lesson: In a three-cornered marketplace, third place doesn't earn profit — it earns the exit press release.

records.name: Sidecar
records.failure_reason: Outspent by Uber and Lyft in the same city
records.investors: Google Ventures, Union Square Ventures, Lightspeed
records.lesson: Being first in a marketplace doesn't help if two better-funded competitors can subsidize both sides longer than you can.

records.name: WeWork
records.failure_reason: Overvaluation & Governance Failure
records.investors: SoftBank, Benchmark, JP Morgan, T. Rowe Price, Fidelity
records.lesson: Confusing a real estate arbitrage business for a tech company enabled a $47B fantasy valuation that collapsed to bankruptcy in 4 years.

records.name: Theranos
records.failure_reason: Fraud & Technology That Never Worked
records.investors: Rupert Murdoch, Betsy DeVos, Walton family, Larry Ellison, Tim Draper
records.lesson: Silicon Valley 'fake it till you make it' collapses on contact with regulated healthcare — biological reality does not bend to press releases.

records.name: Quibi
records.failure_reason: No Product-Market Fit
records.investors: Disney, Alibaba, NBCUniversal, Sony, Viacom, JP Morgan, Goldman Sachs
records.lesson: Raising $1.75B before shipping guarantees you build the wrong product with no way to pivot.

records.name: Juicero
records.failure_reason: Solution In Search Of a Problem
records.investors: Kleiner Perkins, Google Ventures, Campbell Soup
records.lesson: A $400 WiFi-enabled press for juice packs you can squeeze by hand isn't innovation — it's the parody of Silicon Valley excess.

records.name: MoviePass
records.failure_reason: Unsustainable Unit Economics
records.lesson: Charging $9.95/month for a benefit that cost ~$40/month per user was not growth — it was subsidized customer acquisition at company-lethal scale.

records.name: Pets.com
records.failure_reason: Dot-Com Era Overexpansion
records.lesson: Selling 20lb bags of dog food below cost with free shipping in 1999 was less a business than a marketing budget with legs.

records.name: Webvan
records.failure_reason: Overexpansion Ahead of Demand
records.investors: Sequoia, Benchmark, Softbank, Goldman Sachs, Yahoo
records.lesson: Building 26 automated warehouses before proving one worked is the textbook dot-com self-immolation.

records.name: Solyndra
records.failure_reason: Cost Curve Beat by Chinese Silicon
records.investors: US DOE, Argonaut Private Equity, Redpoint, USVP
records.lesson: Betting a hardware startup on commodity prices staying high is a bet against manufacturing gravity — Chinese silicon PV crushed the math.

records.name: Jawbone
records.failure_reason: Outcompeted by Apple, Fitbit and Xiaomi
records.investors: Andreessen Horowitz, Sequoia, Khosla, Kleiner Perkins
records.lesson: Raising $930M as a consumer hardware company chasing three losing categories (Bluetooth headsets, speakers, wearables) is a lesson in strategic drift.

records.name: Homejoy
records.failure_reason: Bad Unit Economics + Worker Misclassification
records.investors: Google Ventures, Redpoint, First Round, Andreessen Horowitz
records.lesson: Subsidizing house cleaning at $19 introductory prices attracts one-time users, not a repeat customer base.

records.name: Beepi
records.failure_reason: Overspending + Poor Unit Economics
records.lesson: Renting a $1.5M office and paying employees Tesla lease bonuses before proving margins is how you incinerate $149M.

records.name: Munchery
records.failure_reason: Poor Unit Economics + Massive Food Waste
records.investors: Menlo Ventures, Sherpa Capital, Sherpa Ventures
records.lesson: Cooking meals speculatively for hoped-for orders throws real food in the trash for hypothetical revenue.

records.name: Kozmo.com
records.failure_reason: Free 1-Hour Delivery of $3 Items
records.investors: Amazon, Starbucks, Softbank, Chase Capital Partners
records.lesson: Free 1-hour delivery of a Snickers bar was never a business — it was an era.

records.name: Boo.com
records.failure_reason: Premature Global Launch + Overbuilt Tech
records.investors: JP Morgan, Bain Capital, Bernard Arnault, Benetton
records.lesson: Launching in 18 countries and 7 languages simultaneously with rich 3D on 56k modems in 1999 is dot-com hubris in one sentence.

records.name: Fab.com
records.failure_reason: Pivot Whiplash + Discount Addiction
records.investors: Andreessen Horowitz, Tencent, Menlo Ventures, Baroda Ventures
records.lesson: Pivoting from a gay social network to flash-sale design retailer to full-price marketplace to just-sell-us-please burns capital and customer trust.

records.name: Rdio
records.failure_reason: Outmarketed by Spotify
records.investors: Skype founders Janus Friis and Niklas Zennström, Mangrove Capital
records.lesson: Better UI and taste didn't outweigh Spotify's distribution deal with Facebook and freemium acquisition machine.

records.name: Napster (1999)
records.failure_reason: Legal Injunctions Killed Product
records.lesson: Building a business on the world's largest infringement of copyrighted music was operating below the law until the law caught up.

records.name: Katerra
records.failure_reason: Vertical Integration Overreach
records.lesson: Trying to redesign every step of a construction supply chain simultaneously guarantees losing money on every step.

records.name: Convoy
records.failure_reason: Freight Recession Killed Take Rates
records.investors: Generation Investment, Baillie Gifford, Bezos Expeditions, Y Combinator
records.lesson: Freight brokerage is a commodity margin business — a $3.8B valuation required a bull market that didn't come.

records.name: Fast
records.failure_reason: Revenue Miss + Founder Spending
records.lesson: A $124M-funded checkout startup with $600k annual revenue is a marketing budget with press releases.

records.name: Blockbuster
records.failure_reason: Disrupted by Netflix + Streaming
records.lesson: Turning down a $50M offer to buy Netflix in 2000 goes in the textbook next to Blockbuster's Chapter 11 filing.

records.name: Toys 'R' Us
records.failure_reason: LBO Debt + Amazon Disruption
records.lesson: A $6.6B leveraged buyout in 2005 saddled Toys R Us with $400M annual interest right as Amazon began eating retail.

records.name: Digg
records.failure_reason: Botched v4 Redesign
records.lesson: A community-first product rebuilt against user protest can lose 50% of active users in a month.

records.name: Grooveshark
records.failure_reason: Copyright Litigation
records.lesson: Uploading unlicensed music to your own service and then arguing DMCA safe harbor never survives contact with major labels.

records.name: Yik Yak
records.failure_reason: Anonymity Enabled Abuse; Removed = No Product
records.lesson: Anonymous location-based apps generate viral growth and abusive content at the same rate — moderation costs became existential.

records.name: Segway (2001-2020)
records.failure_reason: Hype vs Reality Gap
records.investors: Kleiner Perkins, Credit Suisse First Boston
records.lesson: A product Steve Jobs said would 'reshape cities' at $5,000 apiece sold fewer units in a decade than iPhones do in a day.

records.name: Path
records.failure_reason: Failed to Grow Against Facebook + Instagram
records.lesson: A private social network capped at 150 friends couldn't beat Facebook's unlimited graph or Instagram's public content.

records.name: Secret
records.failure_reason: Anonymity Turned Toxic Fast
records.lesson: An anonymous app that raised $25M with insiders selling secondary shares before the growth story broke — then burned out in 16 months.

records.name: MySpace
records.failure_reason: Culture + Product Failure vs Facebook
records.lesson: News Corp bought MySpace for $580M in 2005 and sold it for $35M in 2011 — a 94% loss and Rupert Murdoch's biggest internet miss.

records.name: Friendster
records.failure_reason: Technical Debt + Focus Loss
records.lesson: Friendster invented the social graph and pivoted to gaming, then to social discovery, then died — while MySpace and Facebook won.

records.name: The Messenger
records.failure_reason: Ad Revenue Miss + Executive Overhire
records.lesson: Jimmy Finkelstein's centrist news site raised $50M in 2023, hired 275 people, and closed 10 months later after ~$25M revenue.

records.name: Byte / Clash
records.failure_reason: TikTok Owned the Category
records.lesson: Vine's founder Dom Hofmann tried twice to revive short-form video against TikTok and lost both times.

records.name: Google+
records.failure_reason: Ghost Town + Data Breach
records.lesson: A social network that measured success by force-integration with Gmail rather than user desire folded after one preventable API breach.

records.name: GhostRuck / Zirx / others
records.failure_reason: On-Demand Boom Bust
records.lesson: The 2015 'uber-for-X' cohort — Zirx (parking), GhostRuck (moving), Prim (laundry) — collapsed together as SoftBank money receded.

records.name: Cue Health
records.failure_reason: Post-COVID Demand Collapse + FDA Warning
records.investors: Koch Disruptive Technologies, ACME Capital, Decheng Capital
records.lesson: COVID-era demand for at-home testing masked a diagnostics business without a real everyday use case.

records.name: Brandless
records.failure_reason: Poor Repeat + High CAC
records.lesson: Selling everything for $3 doesn't scale a consumer packaged goods business — it just discounts the CAC into oblivion.

records.name: Scoot Networks
records.failure_reason: Unit Economics + Acquisition Whiplash
records.lesson: Bird acquired Scoot for $25M in 2019 and shuttered US operations 2020 amid COVID — completing the on-demand mobility collapse.

records.name: Better Place
records.failure_reason: Battery-Swap Model Failed
records.lesson: A $200,000-per-station battery-swap network needed EV volumes that Nissan Leaf and one Renault deal couldn't produce.

records.name: Nikola Motors
records.failure_reason: Founder Fraud + Product Delays
records.lesson: Trevor Milton's rolling-truck video demo turned into a securities fraud conviction and a company bankruptcy five years later.

records.name: Juul (partial)
records.failure_reason: FDA Marketing Denial + Litigation
records.lesson: A $38B startup that had Altria buy 35% for $12.8B and then wrote it down to zero as FDA restricted marketing.

records.name: Alikolo
records.failure_reason: Lack of vision and experience
records.lesson: Founders must maintain a clear vision, understand their competitive advantage, and retain sufficient ownership to steer the company's direction and secure future funding.

records.name: Appiterate
records.failure_reason: Acquired by larger company
records.lesson: Successful acquisition can be a positive outcome for a startup, especially when a larger company sees value in its specialized technology and market position to expand its own offerings.

records.name: 37Coins
records.failure_reason: Lack of funds, unreliable technology
records.lesson: Even with an innovative idea, inadequate capital and challenges in core technology implementation can quickly lead to a startup's demise.

records.name: Admazely
records.failure_reason: Lack of funds, key team departures
records.lesson: Securing sufficient funding and retaining key talent are crucial for a startup's survival, especially in the early stages.

records.name: Aria Insights
records.failure_reason: Ahead of market demand, founder departure
records.lesson: Don't build solutions for problems that don't exist on a large enough scale for monetization, and be wary of significant strategic pivots.

records.name: ArsDigita
records.failure_reason: Inexperienced leadership, mismanagement, misguided product changes
records.lesson: Founders must maintain control and strategic vision, especially when bringing in external leadership, to avoid losing focus on core strengths and mismanaging resources.

records.name: BitPass
records.failure_reason: Unable to compete with free alternatives
records.lesson: Disruptive technology with a strong value proposition can quickly render established business models obsolete, especially when free alternatives emerge.

records.name: Brisk
records.failure_reason: Lack of focus, unclear market fit
records.lesson: Broad customization and failing to define a clear customer persona led to product unfocus and ultimately prevented Brisk from finding a sustainable market fit.

records.name: Call9
records.failure_reason: Unsustainable business model, rapid expansion
records.lesson: A novel business model requiring significant behavioral change in a regulated industry like healthcare, especially one that directly impacts physician compensation, faces immense uphill battles and requires robust financial planning.

records.name: Argyle Social
records.failure_reason: Intense competition, insufficient funding, API changes
records.lesson: Even with a good product, intense competition and external platform changes can quickly deplete resources and lead to failure without sufficient funding or effective adaptation.

records.name: Auctionata
records.failure_reason: Legal challenges, unethical practices, mismanagement
records.lesson: Ethical conduct and transparent management are crucial for long-term trust and investor confidence, as a lack thereof can lead to legal issues and ultimately, business failure.

records.name: 99dresses
records.failure_reason: Low revenue, technical debt, poor management
records.lesson: Early-stage startups need to ensure a viable business model from the start and prepare for necessary technical and management growth to sustain operations and scale effectively.

records.name: Circa
records.failure_reason: Lack of funds, unsustainable model
records.lesson: Even innovative news models struggle without a clear, sustainable revenue path, especially when giants can easily replicate and outcompete with established resources.

records.name: Crowdmix
records.failure_reason: Mismanagement of funds, lack of vision
records.lesson: Extravagant spending and lack of product focus can quickly deplete funds, even with significant investment.

records.name: Desti
records.failure_reason: Bad business model with poor revenue generation
records.lesson: Even innovative technology needs a strong, viable business model to generate revenue and survive against established competitors.

records.name: Design Inc.
records.failure_reason: Bad business model, market saturation
records.lesson: Focus on core business essentials, validate assumptions, and continuously optimize the product while fostering experimentation within the team.

records.name: Berg
records.failure_reason: No market need & high price
records.lesson: Even innovative products require a clear market need and a justifiable price point for sustained success.

records.name: Delicious
records.failure_reason: Acquisition Flu
records.lesson: Acquisition by powerful companies can stifle innovation and lead to neglect, allowing competitors to overtake the market.

records.name: ChaCha
records.failure_reason: Competition from AI, high costs
records.lesson: Manually intensive services are difficult to scale and compete with algorithmic solutions when technology advances sufficiently.

records.name: dotCloud
records.failure_reason: Parent company bankruptcy, unsustainable costs
records.lesson: Even successful pivots like Docker can lead to the original product being divested, and its ultimate fate tied to the financial health of its acquiring company.

records.name: Dopplr
records.failure_reason: Loss of value post-acquisition
records.lesson: Acquisitions can sometimes lead to a product's decline if the acquiring company fails to properly integrate or support it, alienating users and halting development.

records.name: EventVue
records.failure_reason: Lack of product-market fit
records.lesson: Even an engaging product can fail if it's a 'nice-to-have' (vitamin) rather than a 'must-have' (painkiller) solution for its primary customers, and doesn't align with their core business needs.

records.name: Flowtab
records.failure_reason: Bad business model, technological failure
records.lesson: A strong business model and robust technology are crucial for success, especially in high-volume, dynamic environments like hospitality.

records.name: CircleBack Lending
records.failure_reason: Bad business model, unpaid loans
records.lesson: P2P lending faces inherent risks from borrower defaults and challenges in distinguishing itself from traditional banking, requiring robust credit assessment and sustainable business models.

records.name: Fab
records.failure_reason: Premature scaling, losing competitive edge
records.lesson: Premature scaling and attempting to replicate another company's success without a solid domestic foundation can lead to significant financial loss and loss of competitive advantage.

records.name: Dinner Lab
records.failure_reason: Unsustainable business model, operational challenges
records.lesson: A novel concept needs a scalable and sustainable business model to succeed, especially in operations-heavy industries where managing numerous variables like staff, locations, and inventory can quickly drain capital and hinder growth.

records.name: Gowalla
records.failure_reason: Lost to Foursquare competition
records.lesson: Focusing on a few core services and excelling at them is often more effective than trying to do too many things at once, especially when facing strong competition.

records.name: Flud
records.failure_reason: Ran out of funding, high competition
records.lesson: Thoroughly test your product and ensure market demand before seeking extensive media coverage to avoid losing credibility due to early technical issues and intense competition.

records.name: Frankly
records.failure_reason: Lack of product-market fit
records.lesson: Even with widespread demand for a product type (like video consumption), a startup can fail if it doesn't achieve sustainable product-market fit, especially when video creation is a barrier for users.

records.name: Dinnr
records.failure_reason: No market need identified
records.lesson: Thorough market research to validate demand is crucial before launching a product, especially if similar alternatives are readily available.

records.name: FoundationDB
records.failure_reason: Acquired by Apple
records.lesson: Acquisitions, especially by tech giants, can lead to the discontinuation of products or services that a community heavily relies on, disrupting an ecosystem.

records.name: Fuhu
records.failure_reason: Mismanagement of funds and high burn rate
records.lesson: Even highly successful companies with a popular product can fail due to severe financial mismanagement and an inability to replicate initial success.

records.name: Formspring
records.failure_reason: Cyberbullying, legal challenges, and lack of monetization
records.lesson: Anonymity without accountability can lead to severe issues like cyberbullying and legal challenges, making a platform unsustainable without a strong moderation and monetization strategy.

records.name: Glitch
records.failure_reason: Bad business model, low player retention
records.lesson: Even innovative products require a viable business model, strong onboarding, and adaptation to evolving technology to achieve broad market adoption and sustainability.

records.name: HiGear
records.failure_reason: Theft and security vulnerabilities
records.lesson: Robust security and fraud prevention measures are critical for peer-to-peer platforms dealing with high-value assets to prevent significant losses and maintain business viability.

records.name: HitMeUp
records.failure_reason: Lack of experience, poor product-market fit
records.lesson: Founders must have or acquire relevant expertise and conduct thorough market validation to ensure product-market fit and effective user acquisition before scaling.

records.name: HubHaus
records.failure_reason: Pandemic and failed Series B
records.lesson: Even with product-market fit, external macro events like a pandemic or investor sentiment shifts can devastate startups, especially those with thin margins and high growth expectations.

records.name: HotelsAroundYou
records.failure_reason: Unable to compete with rivals
records.lesson: New market entrants must demonstrate a strong unique value proposition to overcome established competitors and secure investor confidence for growth.

records.name: Koinex
records.failure_reason: Regulatory ban on cryptocurrency
records.lesson: Startups operating in nascent and unregulated markets face significant risks from adverse regulatory changes, which can swiftly halt operations and render a business unviable, regardless of initial success.

records.name: Kitchit
records.failure_reason: Intense market competition, low margins
records.lesson: Even popular services in competitive markets need strong profit margins and adaptable strategies to survive against well-funded rivals.

records.name: Kno
records.failure_reason: Intense competition from Apple
records.lesson: Even with significant funding and a good idea, intense competition from market giants can quickly diminish a startup's chances of scaling.

records.name: Houseparty
records.failure_reason: Acquired, technology absorbed by Epic Games
records.lesson: Even successful apps can be shut down if they are acquired and their technology is integrated into a larger ecosystem, highlighting the risk of relying on platform-dependent features.

records.name: Kiko
records.failure_reason: Bad management, delayed progress, wrong hires
records.lesson: Focus on your core product, make timely decisions, hire the right team, and involve investors for guidance.

records.name: Leap Transit
records.failure_reason: Regulatory non-compliance, public backlash
records.lesson: Ignoring regulations and local sentiment, even for an innovative service, can lead to swift shutdown and public outcry.

records.name: LayerVault
records.failure_reason: Lack of funds, failed to gain traction
records.lesson: Even with a good product addressing a real need, securing sufficient funding and achieving market traction are critical for long-term survival.

records.name: Justin.tv
records.failure_reason: Pivoted into Twitch, shut down original
records.lesson: Successful pivots can lead to entirely new, more dominant entities, even if the original brand is retired.

records.name: Lookery
records.failure_reason: Over-reliance on third-party platform
records.lesson: Startups heavily reliant on another platform must diversify or be prepared for changes that could undermine their business model.

records.name: Laurel & Wolf
records.failure_reason: Poor operations, customer service, and culture
records.lesson: Chaotic internal operations, poor customer service, and a toxic work culture, even with significant funding, can lead to a startup's demise.

records.name: Move Loot
records.failure_reason: Bad business model, premature scaling
records.lesson: A strong business model and careful validation are crucial before aggressive scaling; expanding too quickly without profitability can be fatal.

records.name: Moped
records.failure_reason: No market need, outdated content
records.lesson: Even with innovative features, a social app needs consistently fresh and engaging content to attract and retain a broad user base in a competitive market.

records.name: Mailbox
records.failure_reason: Acquired, then shut down due to poor integration
records.lesson: Even innovative products face challenges with monetization and integration post-acquisition; a strong business model is crucial for long-term viability even after being acquired.

records.name: MatterFab
records.failure_reason: Poor management, high burn rate, market shift
records.lesson: Even with significant funding and a promising vision, a startup needs stable and experienced leadership, a sustainable burn rate, and adaptability to a rapidly evolving competitive landscape to succeed.

records.name: OpTier
records.failure_reason: Lack of product-market fit (PMF)
records.lesson: Continuously adapt your product to evolving market demands and technological shifts, even if it requires significant investment and re-positioning.

records.name: Lumos
records.failure_reason: Lack of expertise and product-market fit
records.lesson: Founders must deeply understand their target market, product costs, and industry expertise before launching a hardware company, and seek mentorship to avoid common pitfalls.

records.name: Netscape
records.failure_reason: Intense competition from Microsoft
records.investors: Kleiner Perkins; public markets after August 1995 IPO
records.lesson: Even with a groundbreaking product and early market leadership, relentless competition from a dominant tech giant can lead to obsolescence and acquisition.

records.name: Navdy
records.failure_reason: Saturated market, poor product-market fit, high costs
records.lesson: Even with substantial funding, a high price point and products that don't meet customer needs in a saturated market can lead to failure.

records.name: Parse
records.failure_reason: Acquisition led to loss of focus
records.lesson: Acquisitions can lead to a shift in strategic priorities for the acquiring company, potentially sidelining or shutting down the acquired product if it doesn't align with evolving goals.

records.name: Musical.ly
records.failure_reason: Acquired and merged into TikTok
records.lesson: Even highly successful and popular platforms can be absorbed by larger competitors, highlighting the importance of long-term strategic positioning beyond initial user growth.

records.name: PoliMobile
records.failure_reason: No market need, unwilling to pay
records.lesson: Thoroughly validate market demand and willingness to pay before building a product, as even good technology can fail without paying customers.

records.name: Poliana
records.failure_reason: Low market demand, bad business model
records.lesson: Thorough market research and product validation are crucial to ensure demand exists for your offering before investing heavily in development, and be open to pivoting business models if initial attempts fail.

records.name: QBotix
records.failure_reason: Competitor efficiency surpassed innovation
records.lesson: Even innovative technology can fail if competitor improvements make established solutions more cost-effective and market adoption is slower than expected.

records.name: PostRocket
records.failure_reason: Poor product, unreliable, Facebook competition
records.lesson: Startups relying heavily on a major platform must adapt quickly to platform changes and anticipate direct competition from the platform itself.

records.name: Quirky
records.failure_reason: Burned cash, failed to sell enough products
